**Source** [Pathfinder #219: Lord of the Trinity Star](/Sources.aspx?ID=283) pg. 50 **Complexity** Complex The shaft walls vanish and are replaced by an endless field of stars in all direction, as if the viewer were suddenly lost in outer space. --- **Stealth** 30 **Disable** DC 40 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (master) to unweave the magic left in the wake of the Trinity Star’s passage, DC 43 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (expert) to etch temporary runes to siphon away the magic, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (8th rank; counteract DC 33) to counteract the magic; three successes are required to disable the trap. Once the PCs are within the trap’s overwhelming illusion, they can still attempt these checks to disable it, but the check DCs increase by 2. **Moment of Glory** (illusion, mental) **Trigger** A creature moves (or falls) more than 60 feet down the shaft below the illusory throne; **Effect** All creatures in the shaft suddenly witness an endless night sky all around them, as if they were hurtling through outer space with no sign of any nearby planetary bodies. Each affected creature must attempt a DC 40 Will save to resist being [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 (or stupefied 2 on a critical failure) for 24 hours as the visual overwhelms them. The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** **A Voyage Through the Infinite** (1 action) Every round on its turn, the trap inflicts all creatures in the shaft with the perception that they have been hurtling at an unimaginable speed through the vastness of space. The stars are so distant that no indication of movement can be observed or felt beyond that overwhelming mental conviction. At the same time, the creatures feel as if something unimaginably powerful and hungry is chasing them... and gaining on them. Any PC who looks over their shoulder sees that the stars are indeed winking out behind them, as if an immense black object were growing closer or as if the stars themselves were vanishing. While the PC’s body is somehow protected by the vastness of space, their minds are not—each PC must attempt a DC 40 Will save. **Critical Success** As success below, but the creature also realizes they’re reliving the memories of Runelord Xanderghul—like him, they’re escaping some sort of horrific fate and are hurtling toward Golarion. The next time this creature achieves a critical success against this trap, they suddenly see Golarion loom large, and as they witness their “crash” into the Throne of the Troll King, they suddenly wake, prone, in area C1 at the heart Xin-Cyrusian. If any other PCs are still trapped in the Falling Star’s Memories, a PC in Xin-Cyrusian knows instinctively that they can call out to those trapped PCs—each PC in Xin-Cyrusian who does so reduces the save DC against A Voyage Through the Infinite for those still trapped by 5.
**Success** The creature realizes they’re experiencing the path the Trinity Star took through the cosmos and becomes [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.
**Failure** The creature’s grip on reality fades as they experience what seems like years or even decades of hurtling adrift through a vast expanse. The creature becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 24 hours or increases the value of their stupefied condition by 1 if they’re already stupefied.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but stupefied 2 (or increase the stupefied condition by 2). **Special** If this trap would cause a creature’s stupefied condition to exceed stupefied 5, the creature instead “crashes” to the ground on the hilltop outside, about ten feet from the Throne of the Troll King. The creature takes 10d6 bludgeoning damage (DC 40 basic Reflex save), and their stupefied condition now has an unlimited duration. --- **Reset** The trap resets automatically

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 13 **Complexity** Complex A forest of fiendish trees swing their branches and shift their roots to bludgeon and trip creatures in the tainted grove (area A21). --- **Stealth** DC 12 (Trained) to determine the trees can move **Disable** DC 22 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (trained) to find a location the trees can't reach or DC 24 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) to recite a prayer that temporarily casts out the fiendish energy inside a single tree in the grove, disabling it for 1 minute. A disabled or destroyed tree creates a 5-foot-square area in the grove that's safe from this hazard. **AC** 18, **Fort** +14, **Ref** +14 **Hardness** 10 **HP** 40 (BT 20) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Weaknesses** [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 5 **Shift Roots** **Trigger** A creature ends its movement in the grove; **Effect** The trees throughout the tainted grove shift their roots wildly, making the area difficult terrain, then the Abyss-warped trees roll initiative.
**Tighten Grip** **Trigger** The Abyss-warped trees critically hit a creature with a branch Strike; **Effect** The Abyss-warped trees loop their branches around the triggering creature, [grabbing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) it ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 21). --- **Routine** (4 actions) The Abyss-warped trees use their first action each round to lash their roots; each creature in the tainted grove must succeed at a DC 21 Reflex save or fall [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). The Abyss-warped trees use their second, third, and fourth actions to make branch Strikes against up to three different creatures in the tainted grove.
**Melee** branch +14, **Damage** 2d8+5 bludgeoning --- **Reset** The Abyss-warped trees cease moving 1 minute after no living creatures are in the tainted grove. They reset immediately. A disabled tree reanimates after 1 minute. A destroyed tree regrows after 1 month.

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun](/Sources.aspx?ID=259) pg. 34

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A golden guardrail sprays magical, flesh-eating acid throughout the stairwell.

---

**Stealth**
+10 (trained)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) DC 26 (expert) to deactivate the trap’s sensors, or [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) DC 24 (expert) to disrupt the guardrail’s magic, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (3rd rank; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) DC 24) to counteract the guardrail

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 21, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +11

**Guardrail Hardness**
13

**Guardrail HP**
56 (BT 28)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2190), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

</column>

**Spray Acid** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=524), [arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)); **Trigger** A creature steps on the south stairs; **Effect** The guardrail sprays flesh-eating acid, filling the entire stairwell. All living creatures on the stairs area take 2d8+9 acid damage (DC 27 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save). The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its initiative, the trap continues to spray acid, dealing 2d8+9 acid damage to all living creatures on the stairs (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Reflex save).

---
**Reset**
The trap automatically deactivates after 1 minute. It resets in 1 hour.

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=646" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Disgraced Dollmaker](/Sources.aspx?ID=331) pg. 69

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Hidden nozzles in the ceiling spray acid pumped in from a nearby reservoir to destroy the desk and all its documents, as well as anyone trying to retrieve those documents.

---

**Stealth**
+10 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 20 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to disable one of the two acid-spewing nozzles or DC 21 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) (trained) to rig a makeshift plug for one of the two nozzles

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 19, **Fort** +12, **Ref** +6

**Nozzle Hardness**
10

**HP**
22 per nozzle (BT 11)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

</column>

**Ooze Surprise** <actions string="Reaction" /> (acid) **Trigger** A creature flips the switches on the underside of the desk in the wrong order or a creature attempts to open one of the desk drawers without first disabling the trap; **Effect** A hatch opens in the ceiling, releasing a string slime onto the desk. The string slime makes a pseudopod Strike against one creature within reach before rolling initiative. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) The nozzles spray acid from the ceiling onto every creature adjacent to the desk. Each affected creature takes 4d6 acid damage (DC 20 basic Reflex save). For each broken nozzle, this damage is reduced by 2d6.

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates after 1 minute. To be reset, the trap’s reserve tanks must be refilled with acid.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #170: Spoken on the Song Wind](/Sources.aspx?ID=97) pg. 36

**Complexity** Simple

Many carnivorous plants that were once kept satiated now hunger for any meat they can get, even lashing out onto the path to get it.

---

**Stealth**
DC 20 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 25 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (trained) to distract or trick the plants or DC 22 [Nature](/Domains.aspx?ID=22) (expert) to calm the plants

60 (BT 30)

[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)

[acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3) 10, [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 10, slashing 10

</column>

**Trapping Vines** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature moves within reach of the carnivorous plants' vines; **Effect** The vines wrap around the triggering creature. The creature must succeed at a DC 22 Reflex save or be [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 22). Whether or not the creature is grabbed, the plants make a gnawing plants Strike against the creature.

 **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> gnawing plants +17, **Damage** 8d4+12 piecing

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #167: Ready? Fight!](/Sources.aspx?ID=86) pg. 17 **Complexity** Complex A portal to the [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4) rips open onstage, causing roaring winds to tear through the opera house. --- **Stealth** +22 (master) to notice the sudden breeze in the theater **Disable** DC 38 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) (master) to sew the magical threads of the rift shut, DC 40 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (legendary) to open enough windows and doors to reduce its intensity, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (7th level; counteract DC 34) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the air rift **Earth Vulnerability** The Elemental [Plane of Air](/Planes.aspx?ID=4) is opposed by the [Plane of Earth](/Planes.aspx?ID=5). Any spell or magical effect with the [earth](/Domains.aspx?ID=10) trait that targets a creature or area within 50 feet of the rift deals 10 damage to the rift per spell levels (or per 2 levels for magic items, feats, and so forth). For example, a 3rd-level [_earthbind_](/Spells.aspx?ID=94) spell cast on a creature near the air rift deals 30 points of damage to the rift. **AC** 35, **Fort** +30 **HP** 220 **Weaknesses** earth vulnerabilty **Weightlessness** **Trigger** A creature comes within 50 feet of the rift; **Effect** The air rift creates a shroud of [subjective gravity](/Traits.aspx?ID=290) around the creature for 1 minute. The creature can use a free action, which has the [concentrate](/Actions.aspx?ID=683) trait, to choose any direction they wish for gravity to pull them. This allows a creature to Stride along any surface or [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94) in a straight line by choosing a direction into midair. For unattended objects and [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) creatures, this is [microgravity](/Traits.aspx?ID=284): they float in place unless pushed off a surface. --- **Routine** (1 action) Winds blow through the area in a random direction, causing creatures and objects within 50 feet of the air rift to float up, down, north, south, east, or west (roll a d6 to determine which direction). Creatures and objects in the area must attempt a DC 37 Fortitude save. If a creature is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) into a solid object or another creature by this effect, both take 3d8+15 bludgeoning damage on impact.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is pushed 10 feet, but takes only half damage from impact.
**Failure** The creature is pushed 20 feet, falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), and takes full damage from impact.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pushed 40 feet, falls prone, and takes double damage from impact.

**Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 34 **Complexity** Complex A complex device made of multicolored metal that resembles a combination of grinding gears, spider-like legs, and twitching blades, from which emits a constant soft ticking sound. All of the metal in the device appears to be rusted or corroded. --- **Stealth** +8 (trained) **Disable** DC 18 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) to adjust the device's workings so they seize up and no longer function, or DC 21 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) to focus prayers to a non-evil deity into the device to disrupt its ability to channel ambient faith **AC** 18, **Fort** +5, **Ref** +11 **Hardness** 8 **HP** 30 (BT 15) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Spin Up** **Trigger** The ancient apparatus takes damage or an attempt to disable it fails; **Effect** The ancient apparatus begins to grind and churn faster. Its soft ticking whirs up to a discordant buzzing sound, and the entire thing begins to glow with an unsettling rust-colored light. All living creatures in area **D3** experience the unsettling taste of rust in their mouths and must succeed on a DC 18 Fortitude save to avoid becoming [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34). The ancient apparatus then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (3 actions) The ancient apparatus emits beams of rust-colored light, spending an action to make ranged Strikes against three targets in area D3. The apparatus can target creatures as if it possessed [darkvision](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=12), but has no ability to discern between friend or foe. It can't target a creature more than once, and if there are more than three targets, it selects its targets from those it can see in the room randomly. The ancient apparatus has only 1 action as long as its Hit Points are below its BT.
**Ranged** rusty light beam +11 ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)), **Damage** 2d6+5 negative plus [rust creep](/Diseases.aspx?ID=25) --- **Reset** The ancient apparatus reverts to its non-active mode and resets automatically at the end of any round in which there are no obvious targets to attack.

It can't target a creature more than once, and if there are more than three targets, it selects its targets from those it can see in the room randomly. The ancient apparatus has only 1 action as long as its Hit Points are below its BT. Ranged rusty light beam +11 (divine, necromancy), Damage 2d6+5 negative plus rust creep Reset The ancient apparatus reverts to its non-active mode and resets automatically at the end of any round in which there are no obvious targets to attack.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 6" pfs="">[Angry Dead](/Hazards.aspx?ID=405)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #194: Cult of the Cave Worm](/Sources.aspx?ID=209) pg. 38

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The faces of the original dwarven inhabitants of the city appear in the stone and scream in anger.

---

**Stealth**
+18 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to ritually pray for the dead or DC 25 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to exorcise the spirits' anger; a dwarf succeeds at a DC 22 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) check, asking or ordering the spirits to stand down.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Howl of Agony** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16)) **Trigger** At least two living creatures step on the staircase; **Effect** Dozens of mouths open on the stairs and eastern wall doors of the chamber and howl in anger and misery. Creatures in the area are [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=8) for 2 rounds and [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) unless they succeed at a DC 27 Fortitude save. Creatures who critically fail are deafened for 1 minute and frightened 3. The haunt then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) The faces continue to scream, dealing 5d6 sonic damage (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save) to all living creatures within 20 feet of the steps. On a critical failure, a creature takes double damage and is deafened for 1 round. Deaf creatures are immune to this effect.

---
**Reset**
The haunt deactivates 1 round after all living creatures leave the area. After 1 hour, the haunt reactivates. If the haunt is disabled by a [dwarf](/Traits.aspx?ID=54) succeeding at a Diplomacy or Intimidate check, the haunt is destroyed.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 20" pfs="">[Angry Vegetation](/Hazards.aspx?ID=242)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #156: The Apocalypse Prophet](/Sources.aspx?ID=36) pg. 41

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Five large flowers in the weed-choked field unfurl, each dusting pollen onto vines that animate into wemmuths.

---

**Stealth**
DC 42 (master) to notice massive buds beneath the other foliage before they open

**Disable**
DC 48 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) (master) or DC 48 [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) (legendary) to calm a flower, closing it

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 37, **Fort** +33, **Ref** +30, **Will** +30

**HP**
120 per flower

**Immunities**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)

**Weaknesses**
[fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) 20

</column>

**Bloom** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A non-plant creature enters the garden; **Effect** The blooms open, spawning a single [wemmuth](/Monsters.aspx?ID=408) that acts on the hazard's initiative, and the hazard rolls for initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) If there are fewer wemmuths than open flowers, the flowers create more wemmuths (so there as many wemmuths as open flowers) as their first action. For their second action, the flowers produce a mind-addling pollen. Each non-[plant](/Traits.aspx?ID=125) creature within 30 feet of a flower must succeed at a DC 41 Fortitude save or become [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round (or [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) for 1 round, on a critical failure). The pollen is an [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), and [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246) effect.

---
**Reset**
Wemmuths collapse into ordinary vines and the trap resets if the area is left alone for 1 minute.

**Source** [Midnight Burning](/Sources.aspx?ID=346) pg. 189 **Complexity** Complex A spiky iron cage pulls in a victim with animated chains before slamming shut and locking tight. --- **Stealth** +38 (master) **Disable** DC 45 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to [Pick the Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412), DC 48 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (master) to break the lock or bend the bars; five total successes are required to disable the trap **AC** 42, **Fort** +39, **Ref** +30 **Hardness** 35 **HP** 130 (BT 65) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Capturing Chain** **Trigger** A creature that isn’t a member of the inquisition or an authorized ally comes within 15 feet of the cage; **Effect** The trap makes a chain Strike against the triggering creature. If the trap damages and successfully grapples the target with Improved Grab, the trap pulls the target 5 feet closer (or into the cage if the Strike was a critical hit). The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (3 actions) As 1 action, the trap makes a chain Strike against a target in its reach; its Athletics modifier for Improved Grab is +36. The trap can have any number of creatures [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=90) by its chains. If the trap has any creatures grabbed or restrained, it attempts to pull them closer as 1 action with an Athletics check against the creature’s Fortitude DC; on a success, it pulls the creature 5 feet closer (10 feet on a critical success). A Large or smaller creature can be pulled inside the cage, after which the cage door slams shut. The cage can only contain one creature, and that creature is restrained while inside (Escape DC 50). As 1 action, the trap can Constrict the creature inside the cage with more chains.
**Melee** [one-action] chain +38 (magical, reach 15 feet), **Damage** 4d8+20 bludgeoning plus [Improved Grab](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=66)
**Constrict** [one-action] 3d8+20 bludgeoning, DC 45 --- **Reset** The trap deactivates 1 minute after there are no longer any potential prisoners in the room and then activates 1 round after that.

**Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 16 **Complexity** Complex Three pitchers pour water in an endless cascade, each decorated with a symbol of fertility, fecundity, and desire. The pitchers never empty, and the fountain below never overflows; the entire thing flickers with eerie red energy. --- **Stealth** +43 (legendary) to detect the dangerous and sealed entrance to the Eye of Desire; noticing the _anima focus_ itself has a DC of 0 **Disable** DC 50 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (legendary) or [Society](/Skills.aspx?ID=47) (legendary) to decipher the symbols and runes scribed across on the _runewell_ and pinpoint which runes can be used to deactivate it, DC 53 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (legendary) to temporarily disrupt the _anima focus’s_ connection to the Eye of Desire or to destroy a phantom of desire; three total successes are required to disable the hazard (destroying a phantom of desire counts as a single success) **Shroud of Passion’s Might** (mental) **Trigger** A creature attempts to use the _anima focus_ to open the way into the Eye of Desire; **Effect** The _Runewell of Lust’s_ magic reaches out of the Eye of Desire and into the minds of all nearby creatures, creating vivid, dreamlike hallucinations fulfilling their greatest desires. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 44 Will save with the following effects. The hazard then manifests three phantoms of desire—incarnations of Runelord Sorshen empowered by certain beliefs that she hasn’t actually turned over a proverbial new leaf and is playing a long-con game to take over the world. The phantoms and the hazard then roll initiative. **Critical Success** The creature understands the false nature of the hallucination but gleans useful insights from what they see, gaining a +2 status bonus to one Perception check, saving throw, or skill check made before the end of their next turn.
**Success** The creature becomes [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round, then recognizes the hallucination for what it is and blocks it from their mind.
**Failure** The creature becomes lost in the hallucination, struggling to tell it apart from reality. The creature becomes dazzled and [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as long as they remain in Sorshen’s atrium. At the end of each of the creature’s turns, it may attempt a new DC 44 Will save to end this effect.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but slowed 2, and the Will save to end the effect is DC 48. --- **Routine** (1 action) On its turn, the animus of longing sustains the three phantoms of desire. The three creatures each take their turn. --- **Reset** The animus of longing deactivates as soon as no foes remain in the atrium, then immediately resets.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 19" pfs="">[Apocalypse Stormfront](/Hazards.aspx?ID=781)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Mythic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=835" />
<trait label="Nightmare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=961" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 70

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

An endless void stretches in all directions. Visions of Golarion’s destruction roll like storm clouds across the space.

---

**Stealth**
+37 (legendary)

**Disable**
DC 47 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) to Fly through the space without becoming stuck in the webs, DC 50 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) to Climb the webs and make progress forward through the infinite, DC 47 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or DC 50 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (legendary) to collapse the extradimensional space, or DC 52 Perception to peer through the visions of Golarion to notice discrepancies that help keep the overwhelming despair from setting in; six successes disables the hazard, causing it to vanish forever and shunting all creatures to Liralarue’s Prison.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Brewing Storm** <actions string="Reaction" /> (occult) **Trigger** A creature enters the shaft leading to area **C8**; **Effect** Storm clouds roiling with gouts of fire, bolts of lightning, and the wails of uncountable souls form in the distance. The hazard then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) (arcane, emotion, illusion, mental) A stormfront filled with illusory scenes of Golarion’s destruction rolls through the extradimensional space. Each creature in the hazard’s area takes 6d12 mental damage (DC 42 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save). On a failed save, a creature is also [doomed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=67) 1 (doomed 2 on a critical failure). A PC reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is shunted back into area **C7**. A creature that takes damage while Climbing the webs must succeed at a DC 40 Fortitude save or fall. A creature can try to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313) (Reflex DC 40). On a success, they lose one success they’ve earned to escape the hazard but otherwise arrest their fall. On a failure, they plummet into the void, losing all Athletics successes they’ve earned to escape the hazard. Each round on their turn, the character can try to Grab an Edge again, but each time they fail to do so, the party must earn an additional success to escape the hazard. Characters who fall [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) or repeatedly fail to Grab an Edge might effectively become lost in the void, though once the nightmare hazard is disabled, they appear along with the rest of the PCs in Liralarue’s Prison.

---
**Reset**
The hazard resets automatically once no creatures are in the area.

fields.reset: The hazard resets automatically once no creatures are in the area.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 23" pfs="">[Armageddon Orb](/Hazards.aspx?ID=19)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 526

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A roiling red orb, forged from a drop of the god [Rovagug](/Deities.aspx?ID=15)’s blood, rains fire from the sky when a specified condition is met.

---

**Stealth**
DC 10 or [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 48 (legendary) to imbue thieves’ tools with aspects representing [Asmodeus](/Deities.aspx?ID=2) and [Sarenrae](/Deities.aspx?ID=16) and use them to drain away the orb’s power over 10 minutes; the character attempting this check takes 5 fire damage each round until the orb is depleted

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Burn It All** <actions string="Reaction" /> (death, divine, evocation, fire); **Trigger** A special condition set by the trap’s creator occurs; this is typically the event of their death. **Effect** Fire rains from the sky in a 100-mile radius, dealing 10d6 fire damage to creatures and objects in the area. Each creature or object can attempt a DC 46 basic Reflex save. Any creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage dies instantly. This is not enough damage to completely burn away a forest or level an entire mountain or city, but it typically kills most creatures in the area.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 3" pfs="">[Arms of the Drowned](/Hazards.aspx?ID=428)</title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #197: Let the Leaves Fall](/Sources.aspx?ID=222) pg. 35

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Ghostly arms rise up from the water to clutch and grab, while a geyser of leech-infested water sprays up into the central shrine.

---

**Stealth**
+20 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 20 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to offer prayers to calm the haunt, or DC 23 [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) to threaten the unquiet spirits away.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 19, **Fort** +6, **Ref** +12

**HP**
46 (BT 23)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

**Weaknesses**
positive 5

</column>

**Rising Waters** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature swims more than halfway across the river, ends their turn in the bridge shrine, or sets foot onto the northern bridge; **Effect** Ghostly arms rise up from the river to grab and shake both bridges. Creatures standing on the bridge must attempt a DC 20 Reflex save or be knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). A blast of river water sprays up inside the shrine to deposit two [brood leech swarms](/Monsters.aspx?ID=712) in the shrine. The haunt and the leech swarms then roll initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) Ghostly arms flail about and attempt to grab creatures in the shrine or on either bridge. Each round, the haunt uses 3 actions to attempt to [grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=2376) a PC on the bridge or in the shrine. If a PC is restrained, the haunt can use one of its actions to drag a PC into the river. A PC who's restrained in the river risks [drowning](/Rules.aspx?ID=1439).  

**Melee** <actions string="Single Action" />**Melee**  ghostly arms +12, Effect grapple

---
**Reset**
The haunt deactivates and resets at the start of any round in which the PCs aren't in the river, on the bridges, or in the shrines, but the leech swarms remain in the shrine for 10 minutes before retreating back into the water below.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 10" pfs="">[Ash Web](/Hazards.aspx?ID=79)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
<trait label="Fungus" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=77" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #148: Fires of the Haunted City](/Sources.aspx?ID=13) pg. 12

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

This dangerous sooty black mold readily releases its toxic spores when disturbed. The entire swath of fungus in area B2 is a single organism. There are nine 10-foot-square patches to remove, but the whole organism dies once it takes enough damage.

---

**Stealth**
DC 31 (expert)

**Disable**
[Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) DC 27 (expert) to remove a 10-foot-square patch of ash web without triggering the spores

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 28, **Fort** +22, **Ref** +14

**HP**
100

**Immunities**
[acid](/Traits.aspx?ID=3), critical hits, [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=56), [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Spore Explosion** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature moves into the ash web's space or damages the web with any type of damage other than [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) damage. **Requirements** The ash web is not in direct sunlight. **Effect** The triggering creature and all creatures within 10 feet of that creature are exposed to ash web spores.

 **Ash Web Spores** ([inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) The [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) condition from ash web remains even after the poison's duration ends. The condition's value reduces by 1 per hour. [Gugs](/Monsters.aspx?ID=252) are immune to this poison; instead, they have vivid and strange dreams when they sleep after ingesting ash web. **Saving Throw** Fortitude DC 29; **Maximum Duration** 6 rounds; **Stage 1** 2d6 poison damage and enfeebled 1 (1 round); **Stage 2** 4d6 poison damage and enfeebled 2 (1 round); **Stage 3** 6d6 poison and enfeebled 3 (1 round).

---
**Reset**
This large patch of ash web resets automatically at the start of the round.

**Source** [The Final Damnation](/Sources.aspx?ID=347) pg. 193 **Complexity** Complex The edges of the extraplanar tunnel seem to writhe with malevolence, as if preventing unwanted souls from passing through. --- **Stealth** +42 (legendary) **Disable** DC 50 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) (master) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to allow the group to traverse along the portal tunnel; six total successes are required to complete the journey; a PC who succeeds at a DC 48 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36), or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) check as a 2-action activity grants themselves a +2 circumstance bonus to AC and saves against the hazard’s routine for 1 round (on a critical success, they can also grant this bonus to one other PC) **Gaze of Barbatos** (divine, emotion, fear, fire, mental, unholy) **Trigger** A living creature enters the portal tunnel; **Effect** As the PCs begin to pierce planar boundaries, they feel they’ve caught the attention of the archdevil Barbatos, ruler of Avernus. Each creature in the tunnel must attempt a DC 45 Will save. The hazard then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 round and [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=76) 1.
**Failure** The creature is stupefied 2 for 1 minute and frightened 2.
**Critical Failure** The creature is stupefied 3 for 1 minute and frightened 3. --- **Routine** (1 action; divine) The Avernal vortex churns across the portal tunnel, stopping the PCs from reaching their ultimate destination. In the first round, the vortex takes an action to attempt to dispel all beneficial spells on all creatures in the tunnel, scouring them with Hellfire. The vortex has a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) modifier of +43 and a counteract rank of 10, and rolls separately for each spell. On a success, the target creature takes 4d6 fire damage with a DC 45 basic Fortitude save (this has the divine, fire, and unholy traits). In the second round, the vortex attempts to instill a dread of tumbling forever through the tunnel to those within it; each creature takes 6d6 [persistent mental damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) with a DC 45 basic Will save (this is an emotion and mental effect). Once a creature ends its persistent mental damage (or if they avoided the persistent damage), they can reach and escape the tunnel. In all subsequent rounds, the vortex releases bolts of acid, cold, fire, and electricity. It makes one vortex bolt Strike against each creature in the tunnel.
**Ranged** vortex bolt +41 (divine, unholy), **Damage** 4d10+22 acid, cold, fire, or electricity; the damage is chosen randomly, and the Strike gains the appropriate trait; no multiple attack penalty --- **Reset** Once the PCs pass through the portal tunnel and arrive in Hell, the Avernal vortex ends and doesn’t reset.

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #186: Ghost King's Rage](/Sources.aspx?ID=189) pg. 11

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Hundreds of panicked whippoorwills swarm through the area.

---

**Stealth**
+45 (master)

**Disable**
DC 43 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) (master) to calm the birds, DC 45 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (master) to alter your aura, or DC 45 [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) (master) to imitate the living

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Panic!** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Trigger** An [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) or a creature with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) enters the garden; **Effect** The birds screech in panic, dealing 3d12+20 sonic damage to all creatures in the garden (DC 44 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). On a failure, the creature becomes [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) (stunned 3 on a critical failure). The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) The birds swarm wildly through the garden, pecking and slashing at all undead creatures and creatures with negative healing in the garden, dealing 3d10+20 slashing damage and 1d10 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) (DC 44 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save).

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any undead or creatures with negative healing in the garden.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 18" pfs="">[Banshee's Symphony](/Hazards.aspx?ID=29)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 529

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A magically contagious wail of the banshee spell is trapped in the larynx of an invisible, mummified elf.

---

**Stealth**
+30 (legendary)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 42 (master) to pierce the invisible larynx so precisely that the magic releases in a trickle before the trap activates, Thievery DC 44 (legendary) three times to deconstruct the larynx while the trap is active in such a way that it tears the spell apart, or spell DC 38 (9th level) to counteract the [_wail of the banshee_](/Spells.aspx?ID=361) before the trap activates

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Scream** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** Three or more living creatures remain within 100 feet of the trap for 6 seconds or longer. **Effect** The trap releases an arcane wail of the banshee (DC 40) with a 100-foot-radius emanation instead of 40 feet, targeting all living creatures in the area, and rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) The trap uses its action to force one random creature that failed its save against _wail of the banshee_ last turn to emit a _wail of the banshee_ with the same statistics as the initial one. The creature wails even if it is dead or unable to speak, no matter how far away from the trap it is. Unlike a casting of the spell, the drained condition from this trap’s _wail of the banshee_ spells increases the targets’ drained condition values. A creature that critically succeeds at any of its saves can still be affected by the trap on future rounds, but can’t be forced to wail by the trap.

---
**Reset**
The trap ends when the trap is unable to make a creature scream (usually because no creature failed its save on the previous turn or because all creatures have critically succeeded in the past). It then resets over 24 hours, as a new scream builds up in the mummified larynx.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and becomes temporarily immune to the gas for 1 hour, though if the creature has already been stupefied by the trap, that condition remains for its normal duration. Success The creature is unaffected. Failure The creature becomes stupefied 1 for 24 hours. If the target is already stupefied, the condition value increases by 1 (to a maximum of stupefied 4) and the target takes 8d6 mental damage. Critical Effect As failure, except the target takes double the mental damage. Reset After an hour, the trap deactivates; the gas disperses slowly, and the doors can be opened again. After 24 hours, the gas builds up and the trap can be triggered again.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Sweet Tooth](/Sources.aspx?ID=332) pg. 79 **Complexity** Simple A magic circle made of royal icing seals the trap door to the gristmill’s basement shut and plays a nasty trick on anyone who tries to open it without all three of its gumdrop keys. --- **Stealth** DC 10; DC 22 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) to unravel the circle’s meaning without triggering its reaction. **Disable** If the three magical gumdrops which act as this hazard’s keys are placed at the correct points of the magic circle, its enchantment is disabled. Deciphering the correct locations requires a successful DC 20 Arcana or Occultism check; on a critical failure, the mere act of placing the gumdrops activates the Malicious Metamorphosis reaction. Once the enchantment is disabled, the magic circles can be wiped away like any regular icing. **Malicious Metamorphosis** **Trigger** A creature touches the trap door without first placing the three enchanted gumdrop keys in their proper arrangement; **Effect** The magic circles prevent the trap door from opening and maliciously transform a portion of the triggering creature’s body, with effects based on the result of the triggering creature’s DC 18 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The triggering creature is blown 10 feet away from the trap door and knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88), but otherwise unaffected.
**Success** The target is blown 10 feet away from the trap door, knocked prone, and has three fingers on one of their hands transformed into gingerbread. They cannot use weapons with the two-hand or twin traits for as long as the transformation persists.
**Failure** As Success, except the transformation also extends to the creature’s entire hand and a portion of the adjoining arm. The affected creature becomes [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 2 for as long as the transformation persists.
**Critical Failure** As Failure, except the transformation also applies to one of the triggering creature’s legs. For the duration of the transformation, it takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to all of its speeds, is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 and is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58), in addition to the effects listed above. --- **Reset** If the trap door is closed without the magic circles being disturbed, the enchantment resumes as normal.

As an Interact action, a PC can sweep aside some black powder to interrupt the fuse line, but this doesn't prevent Gerhard from activating a keg via blunderbuss. A keg that is removed from its position (either by being thrown over the cliff or merely carried away) retains its explosive potential, but as long as one of the three kegs are removed they no longer have the precise placement required to trigger a collapse—an explosion at this point merely inflicts fire damage in the appropriate areas but does not particularly damage the temple structure itself.   A keg's contents can be dispersed by scattering the gunpowder to the wind (most efficiently by pouring it over the cliff side) as a 2-action activity, or rendered permanently inert by pouring a gallon of water into the powder, inhibiting its explosive qualities. The kegs themselves can be destroyed with damage (note that the AC listed below for each keg takes into account the fact that Gerhard has wedged the kegs into nooks in the temple's stone flooring and walls), but note that any fire damage (including incidental fire damage from area effects like a  fireball  or Gerhard's blunderbuss) causes them to explode. At your option, other actions may be similarly effective at disabling this hazard.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 6" pfs="">[Black Powder Bomb](/Hazards.aspx?ID=68)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #146: Cult of Cinders](/Sources.aspx?ID=7) pg. 40

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

Three bulky kegs of black powder placed at key locations in the temple are triggered to explode in unison, causing the entire structure to collapse into rubble and slide partially down the cliff face.

---

**Stealth**
DC 15 (The three powder kegs aren't particularly well hidden, but they are out of sight to casual observation.)

**Disable**
No special skills are required to disable this manually activated trap. As an Interact action, a PC can sweep aside some black powder to interrupt the fuse line, but this doesn't prevent Gerhard from activating a keg via blunderbuss. A keg that is removed from its position (either by being thrown over the cliff or merely carried away) retains its explosive potential, but as long as one of the three kegs are removed they no longer have the precise placement required to trigger a collapse—an explosion at this point merely inflicts fire damage in the appropriate areas but does not particularly damage the temple structure itself.

 A keg's contents can be dispersed by scattering the gunpowder to the wind (most efficiently by pouring it over the cliff side) as a 2-action activity, or rendered permanently inert by pouring a gallon of water into the powder, inhibiting its explosive qualities. The kegs themselves can be destroyed with damage (note that the AC listed below for each keg takes into account the fact that Gerhard has wedged the kegs into nooks in the temple's stone flooring and walls), but note that any [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) damage (including incidental fire damage from area effects like a [_fireball_](/Spells.aspx?ID=119) or Gerhard's blunderbuss) causes them to explode. At your option, other actions may be similarly effective at disabling this hazard.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 26, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +8

**Hidden Keg Hardness**
5

**Hidden Keg HP**
20 (BT 10)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

**Weaknesses**
[fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) automatically penetrates hardness

</column>

**Destructive Explosion** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72)); **Trigger** One of the three kegs takes any fire damage, including damage caused by a line of black powder burning up to a keg. **Effect** The keg explodes, causing 5d6 fire damage (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex) in a 20-foot emanation; this can cause an instantaneous chain reaction if either of the other kegs are in this area (note that as positioned, all three kegs are in range to trigger a chain reaction). Fire damage in overlapping areas isn't cumulative, but if all three kegs are in their initial positions when the explosion occurs, the temple itself collapses, causing 8d6 bludgeoning damage to all creatures in the temple (DC 24 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex).

**Source** [The Cellars](/Sources.aspx?ID=360) pg. 76 **Complexity** Complex The walls and ceiling begin bleeding more and more, and gouts of cursed blood spew from both decapitated statues’ necks. --- **Stealth** +13 (expert) **Disable** DC 23 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) to exorcise the influence of Charg from a statue, DC 26 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) to dismantle the magical blood generator in a statue’s neck, [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (3rd-rank, [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) DC 20) to render a statue inert; each statue must be disabled separately **AC** 22, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +9 **Statue Hardness** 12 **HP** 50 (BT 25) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Let The Walls Weep Blood** **Trigger** A non-sahkil creature moves more than 10 feet into area **C13**; **Effect** The walls and ceiling begin to weep blood at an alarming rate, causing the floor of area **C13** to grow slick. A non-sahkil that moves across the slick floor is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) and must [Balance](/Actions.aspx?ID=2369) (DC 20 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34)) as long as the hazard remains active. An area of effect with the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555) trait created in this area freezes the blood on the floor, making it even more slippery (increasing the Acrobatics check to Balance to DC 22). The hazard then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (2 actions) The hazard sprays a sizzling gout of cursed blood from the neck stumps of each of the defiled statues of Pharasma for each of its actions. If a statue is disabled or destroyed, the hazard loses that corresponding action. Each gout targets a randomly determined non-sahkil creature in area **C13**, who must then attempt a DC 22 Reflex save against the following effects. After dark, this trap gains 4 actions instead of 2, with each statue firing two gouts of blood. Regardless of how many gouts are fired, a creature can be targeted only once per round by these gouts. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes 2d6 spirit damage.
**Failure** The target takes 2d8 spirit damage, 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), and is exposed to the curse of death’s blood.
**Critical Failure** The target takes 4d8 spirit damage, 2d6 persistent bleed damage, and is exposed to the curse of death’s blood (and takes a –2 circumstance penalty to save against the curse).
**Curse of Death’s Blood** (curse, divine) **Saving Throw** DC 22 Fortitude; **Effect** Your blood grows cold and imbued with death. Whenever you are struck by a critical hit, you take an additional 1d6 [persistent bleed damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86), and as long as you are taking persistent bleed damage, you become [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 1 as your body weakens under the lure of death’s embrace. If you make your daily preparations at a location sanctified to Pharasma or Shelyn (such as area **A9** after Shirail’s phantom returns), you can attempt a new saving throw to end this curse. --- **Reset** The blasphemous blood deactivates at the start of any round in which no creatures other than a sahkil are in area **C13**, then resets after 3 rounds.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #165: Eyes of Empty Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=81) pg. 45

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A hard-to-reach rune is placed on the lock’s tumbler. It emits a blast of force when the door is jostled.

---

**Stealth**
DC 32 (master)

**Disable**
DC 32 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to disarm the rune, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (5th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) DC 28) to counteract the rune’s magic.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Force Blast** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=610), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662)) **Trigger** A non‑[undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=722) creature opens the door or critically fails an attempt to disarm or dispel the rune; **Effect** A 30‑foot [cone](/Rules.aspx?ID=2386) of force issues forth from the lock. Creatures within the cone must succeed a DC 29 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude saving throw or take 8d12 force damage. Those who fail the save are pushed 10 feet, and those who critically fail are pushed 20 feet and are [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 2.

---
**Reset**
The rune resets 1 minute after it triggers.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun](/Sources.aspx?ID=259) pg. 37

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A tiny spark of [Nin’s](/Deities.aspx?ID=353) will drains the blood from living intruders.

---

**Stealth**
+15 (trained)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) DC 26 (expert) to vandalize the space, or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) DC 24 (expert) to pray to a god for passage, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (3rd rank; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=2250) DC 25) to counteract the magical energy

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Drain Blood** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510)); **Trigger** A living creature enters the room of their own accord; **Effect** The trap drains the blood from all living creatures in the room, which manifests as a bloody mist in the air. All living creatures in the room are dealt 2d6+8 void damage (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On a failure, a creature increases the value of their [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its initiative, the trap continues to drain blood, dealing 2d6+8 void damage to all living creatures in the room (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On a failure, a creature increases the value of their [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) condition by 1.

---
**Reset**
The trap automatically deactivates after 1 minute. It resets in 1 hour.

Beams of cold blue light shine from Belcorra’s eyes and open mouth, causing blisters and decay to spread across flesh. Living creatures within a 30-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) from the center of area A11 must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save. The haunt then rolls initiative.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 1d8 negative damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 1d8+6 negative damage and is [dazzled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=65) for 1 round.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 2d8+6 negative damage and is [blinded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=59) for 1 round then dazzled for 1 round. --- **Routine** (1 action) The bloody image opens its mouth and appears to inhale, drawing blood from the body of one creature in its line of sight within 90 feet from the center of area A11. The creature targeted must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save.
**Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 1d10 [bleed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) damage.
**Failure** The creature takes 1d10+6 bleed damage.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes 2d10+6 bleed damage and is [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=71) 2 as long as it’s bleeding. --- **Reset** If the haunt is disabled or destroyed through damage, the bloody phantom of Belcorra sprays upward in a spiral, dousing the trap door leading to area **A25** before draining upward through the keyhole, which reduces the Thievery DC to [Pick the Lock](/Actions.aspx?ID=2412) to 20. At the next sunrise, the blood drains back down to this room and the haunt resets. The haunt is destroyed permanently once Lasda Venkervale is rescued from area **D9**.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 0" pfs="">[Blood-Soaked Soil](/Hazards.aspx?ID=134)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 64

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

The blood of those who died in the area bubbles up from the earth, soaking the soil and turning it into a bloody morass.

---

**Stealth**
DC 16 (trained) to smell blood

**Disable**
DC 18 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to settle the spirits or DC 19 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to bless the area

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Seep Blood** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [earth](/Traits.aspx?ID=55), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** A creature enters the area; **Effect** Blood seeps up from the earth, turning the area into sucking, gory mud. The area becomes difficult terrain for 1 hour. All creatures in or moving through the area must succeed at a DC 16 Reflex save, or they become [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until they can [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) (DC 16).

---
**Reset**
1 day

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 524 **Complexity** Simple An object haunted by the echoes of a vicious mind attempts to kill someone who comes near. --- **Stealth** DC 31 (trained) **Disable** [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) DC 29 (master) to exorcise the spirit or [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) DC 31 (expert) to talk it down **Quietus** (death, emotion, fear, illusion, mental, occult); **Trigger** A creature moves within 10 feet of the haunted object. **Effect** The haunt takes control of the triggering creature, forcing it to attack itself. The creature must attempt a DC 29 Will save. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target makes a Strike against itself and automatically hits; the target also becomes [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).
**Failure** The target makes a Strike against itself and automatically scores a critical hit; the target also becomes [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19).
**Critical Failure** The target attempts a Fortitude save. If the target succeeds, it is subject to the effects of a failure instead. If the target fails, it is reduced to 0 Hit Points and dies.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 5" pfs="">[Blooming Jijioa](/Hazards.aspx?ID=339)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #187: The Seventh Arch](/Sources.aspx?ID=192) pg. 76

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

An invisible solar fare causes this patch of unassuming ground cover to suddenly bloom into a radioactive feld.

---

**Stealth**
DC 26 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 22 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) (trained) to remove a 5-foot square of jijioa, or 5 points of fire damage to destroy an affected area

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 25, **Fort** +17, **Ref** +9

**HP**
52 (BT 26)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

**Weaknesses**
fire 10

</column>

**Solar Bloom** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** The jijioa patch is exposed to a solar flare; **Effect** The countless jijioa fowers suddenly bloom, magnifying the ambient heat of the sun a hundredfold. Creatures in the jijioa patch take 4d6 fire damage (DC 22 basic Fortitude save). Creatures that end their turn in the patch continue to take damage in this way as long as the jijioa is in bloom.

---
**Reset**
 An hour after blooming, a jijioa patch goes dormant for 1 week.

Four pressure plates beneath the floorboards activate dragon-headed fountains on either side of the room, which spray boiling water across the area between them.

---

---

Once a pressure plate has been activated, it must be reset manually

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 14" pfs="">[Boneburst](/Hazards.aspx?ID=464)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Unholy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=521" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [War of Immortals](/Sources.aspx?ID=232) pg. 209

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A low howl rises from the ground, gathering strength as scraps of ancient armor, bone fragments, and clumps of earth rise into the air. Crimson vapor holds the faceless shape together, never coalescing into an identifiable form, but merely writhing through ever-changing images of torment and destruction.

---

**Stealth**
+38 (master) to notice that clouds of debris are coalescing into swirling, faceless shapes held together by rust-red fog and spectral, dripping clots of gore

**Disable**
DC 38 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (master) to temporarily negate the psychic resonances around each fragment, causing the agglomeration to fall apart, or DC 33 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (expert) to temporarily interrupt [Verex-That-Was's](/Monsters.aspx?ID=3409) unholy power with divine energy from another source. If a boneburst takes 40 points of damage from a single source and it isn't destroyed, it is rendered dormant for 1 round.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 33, **Fort** +30, **Ref** +28

**Hardness**
20

**HP**
90 (BT 45)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Gathering Mist** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A living creature approaches within 50 feet of a dormant boneburst; **Effect** The boneburst awakens, roiling up from the ground, and rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) An awakened boneburst occupies a 20- foot square; it is reduced to a 10-foot square when it reaches its BT. It can occupy the same space as other creatures, but not other bonebursts. On its initiative, the boneburst [Flies](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) up to 30 feet toward the nearest living creature as its first action. As its second action, the boneburst then coalesces around any living creature within its space, invisible shards of bone tearing at their flesh. Each living creature in its space takes 2d10+18 slashing damage and 1d10 spirit damage (DC 35 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). If no living creatures are within its space, the boneburst can use its second action to Fly up to 30 feet.

---
**Reset**
If the boneburst spends 5 consecutive rounds without coalescing around a living creature, it falls dormant, sinking back into the earth. After it falls dormant or is disabled, the boneburst gathers energy over the course of the next hour, after which it can be triggered again.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 9" pfs="">[Bottomless Pit](/Hazards.aspx?ID=11)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 524

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

An iron trapdoor covers an infinitely deep 10-foot-square pit.

---

**Stealth**
DC 30 (or 0 if the trapdoor is disabled or broken) or [_detect magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=66)

**Disable**
[Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 28 (trained) to remove the trapdoor

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 28, **Fort** +12, **Ref** +12

**Trapdoor Hardness**
9

**Trapdoor HP**
36 (BT 18)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Infinite Pitfall** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature walks onto the trapdoor. **Effect** The triggering creature falls in and continues to fall, potentially forever. That creature can try to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) to avoid [falling](/Rules.aspx?ID=402). The DC to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) the walls or Grab an Edge is 26.

 The pit contains many handholds, so the falling creature can try to Grab an Edge again every 6 seconds. If the creature succeeds, it can start to Climb out from that point (though it might be a very long climb, depending on how far the creature fell). Since the creature falls endlessly, it can rest and even prepare spells while falling, though items dropped while falling are usually lost forever.

---
**Reset**
The trap still causes creatures to fall forever if they fall in, but the trapdoor must be reset manually for the trap to become hidden again.

<column gap="tiny">

A weight-sensitive plate buried underneath sand pulls a boulder over a cliff ledge, causing it to fall on targets within the entrance.

---

Resetting the boulders in the trap is a labor-intensive project that takes 2 hours.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 13" pfs="">[Bounding Hounds](/Hazards.aspx?ID=193)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 125

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Three phantom hounds chase down intruders, damaging any they pass through.

---

**Stealth**
DC 37

**Disable**
DC 36 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) (expert) to calm each hound, or DC 38 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (master) to banish each hound

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 34, **Fort** +20, **Ref** +26, **Will** +20

**HP**
60 per hound

**Resistances**
all damage 10 (except [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297), or [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128); double resistance to non-[magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103))

</column>

**Bay** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([evocation](/Traits.aspx?ID=65), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=147)) **Trigger** A creature enters the area; **Effect** The hounds manifest and bay loudly, dealing 3d10+16 sonic damage to all creatures within 30 feet of the hounds (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). On a failed check, a creature is additionally [frightened 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19). The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(9 actions) The trap loses 3 actions each round for each hound disabled. Each hound uses three actions to Stride 40 feet after creatures in the room, passing through corporeal creatures during this movement if possible. Each creature the hound moves through during its movement takes 2d8+7 negative damage (DC 37 Reflex negates). A creature can only be damaged by each hound once each round, no matter how many times the hound moves through their space.

---
**Reset**
1 hour

**Source** [Kingmaker Adventure Path](/Sources.aspx?ID=150) pg. 133 **Complexity** Complex The faces carved on the wall appear to inhale, then exhale slithering tendrils of darkness to harm those who would despoil the tomb. --- **Stealth** +13 (trained) **Disable** Thievery DC 23 (expert) to disarm the trap's sensors in the chamber floor, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (3rd level; counteract DC 23) to counteract the faces. Breaking one of the faces on the walls reduces the trap's save DC, attack rolls, and its total actions by 1 per broken face; if all four faces are destroyed, the trap is disabled. **AC** 22, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +9 **Face Hardness** 12 **Face HP** 30 (BT 15) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Draining Inhalation** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** A non-flying living creature moves more than 10 feet into area **C2**; **Effect** Each face inhales then exhales, and all living creatures in area **C2** feel their strength and vitality being drawn out of them as tendrils of shadow from the faces latch onto their bodies. Each creature must succeed at a DC 22 Fortitude save or become [enfeebled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=13) 1 (enfeebled 2 on a critical failure). --- **Routine** (4 actions) The trap loses 1 action per disabled face each turn. On each action, a different face spews a writhing breath of darkness from its mouth to a target in area C2. A creature can only be targeted once per round by the despairing breath, so if fewer than four creatures are in the room, the trap won't be able to take full advantage of all four of its actions.
**Ranged** despairing breath +17 ([fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)), **Damage** 2d8+7 mental damage; no multiple attack penalty. A creature damaged by the despairing breath must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or become [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) 1 (or [fleeing](/Conditions.aspx?ID=17) 1 on a critical failure); this effect has the [fear](/Traits.aspx?ID=68) trait. --- **Reset** The trap resets after 1 minute.

**Source** [Springing Sarini Manor](/Sources.aspx?ID=315) pg. 150 **Complexity** Complex A 10-foot-wide patch of dead shrubs with wilted flowers steals the breath of the living. --- **Stealth** +15 (expert; or –10 and no minimum proficiency if the thicket has been recognized) **Disable** DC 28 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) (expert) or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) (expert) to recognize the thicket for what it is and avoid it **AC** 15, **Fort** +18, **Ref** +11 **Hardness** 15 **HP** 58 (BT 29) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2190), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Weaknesses** fire 15 **Branch Ambush** **Trigger** A creature that breathes steps within 5 feet of a thicket; **Effect** The thicket makes a sinewy leaves Strike against the triggering creature. The hazard then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (3 actions) The breathless thickets patch attempts to Strike a creature in its reach. It then uses Suffocate if it has any creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77); otherwise, it continues to Strike. **Melee** [one-action] sinewy leaves +20 (reach 10 feet) **Effect** branch grab
**Branch Grab** If the breathless thicket hits a creature with its leaves, that creature becomes grabbed by the thicket. Unlike with a normal Grab, the creature isn't immobilized, but it can't move beyond the reach of the thicket's leaves. A creature can sever a branch by Striking against AC 18 and dealing at least 12 slashing damage. A branch doesn't have the thicket's Hardness, and damaging it doesn't deal damage to the thicket. The DC to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) a branch is 26.
**Suffocate** ([incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=661)) **Requirements** The breathless thicket has grabbed one or more creatures that breathe; **Effect** The dead flowers of the breathless thicket begin pulling oxygen from its victims' lungs. Each creature grabbed by the breathless thicket takes 4d6 nonlethal bludgeoning damage and must attempt a DC 26 Fortitude save. **Critical Success** The creature takes no damage and can immediately attempt to Escape (DC 26) as a free action.
**Success** The creature takes half damage and is [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage, is stupefied 1 for 1 round, and is [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1. For as long as it's grabbed by the thicket, the creature must hold its breath or [suffocate](/Rules.aspx?ID=2439).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature also falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=95) and starts suffocating. If it’s no longer grabbed, the creature stops suffocating. --- **Reset** The thicket goes back into hibernation 1 round after there are no more targets to Strike in its reach. It then remains dormant for 24 hours.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 6" pfs="">[Bring Dusk To Dawn](/Hazards.aspx?ID=753)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=622" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Haunted Shore](/Sources.aspx?ID=358) pg. 41

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Shadows rise up from the empty tub, creeping along the floor, walls, and celling to blot out light.

---

**Stealth**
+18 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 25 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) or [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) (expert) to burn out the shadowy influence through prayer or meditation, DC 28 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (trained) to use magic to block the shadowy influence from being able to manifest at all; three successes are required to disable the haunt.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 24, **Fort** +11, **Ref** +14, **Will** +17

**Shadowy Figure HP**
100 (BT 50)

**Immunities**
bleed, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), precision damage

**Weaknesses**
vitality 5

**Resistances**
all 5 (except force, _ghost touch_, spirit, or vitality; double resistance against non-magical)

</column>

**Shadows Rise** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** More than three living creatures end their turn in area **A19** or any one creature ends their turn while standing within the empty bath; **Effect** Shadows seep out from the bath and swiftly coat the walls and ceiling, covering all entrances into **A19** with sheets of shadow, plunging the area within into darkness. Non-magical light sources, such as a torch or lantern, do not emanate any light in the room while the haunt is active. This also suppresses magical light of rank 3 or lower. The haunt then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) A shadowy figure rises up from the bath, resembling the upper torso of a demonic humanoid with glowing eyes. On its first action, the haunt sweeps its many arms through area **A19**, dealing 4d6 void damage on all living creatures in the area (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On its second action, it either spawns an undead shadow from its mass, or it Sustains a currently spawned undead shadow; it can only have one shadow active at a time. This shadow has the minion trait, cannot leave area **A19**, and takes its two actions on the haunt’s initiative. Void damage from the haunt doesn’t heal a shadow minion.

---
**Reset**
The haunt deactivates at the end of any round in which no living creature is in area **A19**, then resets 1 round later.

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 15 **Complexity** Complex Ghostly attackers knock the tables about, send dishes flying, and pull fleeing creatures into the room. --- **Stealth** +20 (trained) **Disable** DC 34 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (expert) to say an [Iroran](/Deities.aspx?ID=10) prayer and put the haunt temporarily to rest, DC 38 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (master) to create a ward against future hauntings **Ghostly Pull** **Trigger** One round passes since a creature entered the refectory; **Effect** A Broken Rebus monk grabs the creature and yanks them toward the room's center. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 36 Fortitude save. The haunt can use this reaction any number of times per round, but only once per creature that tries to leave the room. The haunt then rolls initiative, if it hasn't already. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [pulled](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) 10 feet into the room.
**Failure** The creature is pulled 15 feet into the room.
**Critical Failure** The creature is pulled 15 feet into the room, knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31), and takes 2d6 bludgeoning damage. --- **Routine** (1 action) The haunt sends a flurry of objects hurtling across the room. All creatures in the room are battered by the ghostly objects, taking 3d10+14 force damage (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates after 1 minute. It re-forms at the same times every day, 7 a.m. and 7 p.m., which is when the monks had their morning and evening meals. If at least two people cook a meal in the kitchen, share a meal in the refectory, and utter a prayer to Irori before the meal, the haunt becomes permanently disabled and doesn't re-form.

fields.markdown:
<title level="1" right="Hazard 13" pfs="">[Brooding Fvalthahalia](/Hazards.aspx?ID=169)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Shadows at Sundown](/Sources.aspx?ID=121) pg. 42

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

Tiny black flames mirror living creatures' movements in the city above as scraps of shadow patrol the streets—flames that notice intruders in their “sky” below and reach out to the intruders "above" with a deafening violence that incidentally alerts several of the vault's denizens to the intruders' presence.

---

**Stealth**
DC 37 (master)

**Disable**
DC 40 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to adjust the model so its attention is focused inward, DC 37 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (expert) to cause the accumulated psychic energy to discharge harmlessly, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (7th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 32). A character who sneaks through the room with a DC 32 [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) (expert) check avoids triggering the hazard, but this does not disable it.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Call of Fvalthahalia** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([abjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=2), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** A creature without supernatural ties to the [Shadow Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=11) enters the room (creatures like [fetchlings](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=30) or divine spellcasters who worship [Zon-Kuthon](/Deities.aspx?ID=20) represent two examples of creatures who won't trigger this hazard); **Effect** The flickering dark flames on the city's streets flare up and the sound of an entire city populace screaming an alarm fills the room. All creatures in area C1 take 18d6 sonic damage (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save), and all strigoi from Aliriel's Vault immediately know intruders have been spotted in this room. Any strigoi in area C2 quickly investigate and attack the PCs on sight.

---
**Reset**
1 hour

Stealth DC 37 (master) Disable DC 40 Thievery (master) to adjust the model so its attention is focused inward, DC 37 Occultism (expert) to cause the accumulated psychic energy to discharge harmlessly, or dispel magic (7th level; counteract DC 32). A character who sneaks through the room with a DC 32 Stealth (expert) check avoids triggering the hazard, but this does not disable it. Call of Fvalthahalia Reaction (abjuration, occult) Trigger A creature without supernatural ties to the Shadow Plane enters the room (creatures like fetchlings or divine spellcasters who worship Zon-Kuthon represent two examples of creatures who won't trigger this hazard); Effect The flickering dark flames on the city's streets flare up and the sound of an entire city populace screaming an alarm fills the room. All creatures in area C1 take 18d6 sonic damage (DC 33 basic Fortitude save), and all strigoi from Aliriel's Vault immediately know intruders have been spotted in this room. Any strigoi in area C2 quickly investigate and attack the PCs on sight. Reset 1 hour
