**Source** [Pathfinder #221: Into the Apocalypse Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=371) pg. 62 **Complexity** Complex Queen Sorshen is a beautiful Thassilonian woman wielding a shimmering guisarme. Her violet eyes are fierce and focused, but the corner of her lips twist up in a small, lopsided smile. --- **Stealth** +45 for initiative; noticing her has a DC of 0 **Disable** DC 55 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) to unravel the energies allowing Sorshen to continue to vex Xanderghul; 4 successes are required to disable the hazard. **AC** 51, **Fort** +33, **Ref** +39, **Will** +43 **Hardness** 40 **HP** 164 (BT 82) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Ally of Golarion** **Trigger** Xanderghul rolls initiative; **Effect** Sorshen casts telepathy, allowing her to communicate with the PCs; she can inform them of her options during her routine and follows their advice and requests if given. She then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (3 actions) On her initiative each round, Sorshen can spend her three actions on any of the following options, following PC suggestions if requested. She cannot use any action from the following list more than once per round.
  • **Aid Ally** Sorshen uses her magic to empower one of the PCs, granting that PC a +4 circumstance bonus to attack rolls until the start of her next turn.
  • **Dispel Pride** Sorshen attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) a magic effect put in place by Xanderghul, with a counteract rank of 9th and a +40 modifier for the roll.
  • **Distracting Presence** Sorshen uses her power to distract Xanderghul, causing him to lose his resistance to mental damage until the start of her next turn and also to attempt a DC 50 Will save with the following results. **Critical Success** Xanderghul takes no further penalty, and is temporarily immune to Distracting Presence for 24 hours.
    **Success** Xanderghul is [off-guard](/Conditions.aspx?ID=58) until the start of his turn.
    **Failure** Xanderghul is off-guard until the start of Sorshen’s next turn.
    **Critical Failure** As failure, but Xanderghul is also [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as long as he remains off-guard.
  • **Indulgent Arcana** Sorshen empowers a PC's magic, so that the next spell with the [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647) trait they cast before Sorshen's next turn increases its save DC and attack roll by 2 and removes the spell's incapacitation trait, if any.
  • **Sinuous Strike** Sorshen swings her guisarme, usurping some of Xanderghul's own power to manifest an illusory duplicate that attempts a guisarme Strike against him.
    **Melee** guisarme +44 (magical), **Damage** 4d10+26 slashing

<title level="1" right="Hazard 3" pfs="">[Quicksand](/Hazards.aspx?ID=22)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 526

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A 15-foot-wide patch of water and sand attempts to submerge creatures that step onto it.

---

**Stealth**
+12 (trained) (or –10 and no minimum proficiency if the surface is disturbed)

**Disable**
[Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) DC 18 (trained) to disturb the surface

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Submerge** <actions string="Free Action" /> **Trigger** A Huge or smaller creature walks onto the quicksand. **Effect** The triggering creature sinks into the quicksand up to its waist. The quicksand rolls initiative if it hasn’t already.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its initiative, the quicksand pulls down each creature within it. A creature that was submerged up to its waist becomes submerged up to its neck, and a creature that was submerged up to its neck is pulled under and has to hold its breath to avoid [suffocation](/Rules.aspx?ID=468).

 A creature in the quicksand can attempt a DC 20 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Swim](/Actions.aspx?ID=39) to either raise itself by one step if it’s submerged to its neck or worse, or to move 5 feet if it’s submerged only up to its waist. On a critical failure, the creature is pulled down one step. A creature that Swims out of the quicksand escapes the hazard and is [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) in a space adjacent to the quicksand patch. Other creatures can [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) the creature, typically by using a rope or similar aid, or attempt to pull the creature out with their own DC 20 Athletics check, with the same results as if the creature attempted the check.

---
**Reset**
The hazard still submerges anyone who walks in, but the surface doesn’t become hidden again until it settles over the course of 24 hours.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 8" pfs="">[Rage of the Sky Father](/Hazards.aspx?ID=557)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=161" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane
](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 7

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Ominous storm clouds gather overhead, pulsating with flashes of blue-white lightning.

---

**Stealth**
+18 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (trained) to petition [Gozreh](/Deities.aspx?ID=284) for safe passage or 28 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) to disperse the storm’s magical energies. A PC whose voice is exceptionally loud (such as using the [_bullhorn_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1971) cantrip) can also attempt to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) this hazard with a DC 25 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=39) check to convince the Gozren priests that they mean no harm; the priests make a second prayer to dissipate the hazard on the following round, though they’re unable to stop the sargassum heaps.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Thunderclap** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [sonic](/Traits.aspx?ID=697)) **Trigger** A creature not designated by Katlanthe approaches within 10 feet of the circle of stone columns; **Effect** The storm clouds release a boom of thunder. Creatures atop the plateau take 2d10+9 sonic damage (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). On a critical failure, the creature is also [deafened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=66) for 1d4 rounds. The hazard rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [electricity](/Traits.aspx?ID=586)) A bolt of lightning strikes a 10-foot [burst](/Rules.aspx?ID=2385) atop the plateau of the GM’s choosing. Creatures in the area take 2d10+9 electricity damage (DC 28 Reflex save). On a critical failure, the creature is also [stunned](/Conditions.aspx?ID=93) 1. Creatures designated by Katlanthe within the area are infused with divine energy for 1 round. They gain the electricity trait and [immunity](/Rules.aspx?ID=2312) to electricity damage, and all their attacks deal an additional 1d6 electricity damage.

---
**Reset**
The storm clouds disperse once no creature other than those designated by Katlanthe are atop the plateau.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 5" pfs="">[Ravenous Pit](/Hazards.aspx?ID=676)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Devils of Chitterwood](/Sources.aspx?ID=310) pg. 54

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

 A seemingly ordinary hole in the forest floor exerts a strange gravity on creatures that come near.

---

**Stealth**
+13 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) three times to disperse the unusual energy surrounding the hole, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (3rd rank; counteract DC 22) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the engulfing magic

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Deadly Inhale** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature approaches within 15 feet of the hole; **Effect** The ravenous pit seems to “inhale,” attempting to pull creatures into itself. Each creature within 15 feet must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude save. On a failure, the creature is pulled 5 feet closer to the hole (10 feet on a critical failure). The pit then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) For each action, the pit chooses a different creature within a 20-foot emanation to attempt to swallow. That creature must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save. On a failure, the creature is pulled 5 feet closer to the hole (10 feet on a critical failure). If this would pull the creature into the pit, that creature can attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313) as a reaction (DC 22). A creature who falls into the pit disappears into an extradimensional space that feels like being buried alive. A creature takes 2d8+7 bludgeoning damage (DC 20 basic Fortitude save) at the end of each its turns in the extradimensional space. A creature in this extradimensional space is [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) and [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1; they can Escape this extradimensional space with a successful DC 22 Athletics, Nature, or Survival check. If they succeed, they appear in a random spot no more than 10 feet from the hole as if they had clawed their way from the dirt.

 While this trap is active, all creatures treat movement away from the pit as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366).

---
**Reset**
If the trap isn’t disabled, it becomes dormant for 10 minutes if there are no creatures within 20 feet of it at the start of its turn.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #153: Life's Long Shadows](/Sources.aspx?ID=29) pg. 25

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

The restless spirit of Currew raves against his tormentors when someone enters his room.

---

**Stealth**
+20 (expert) or DC 30 (master) to detect the spiritual nexus

**Disable**
DC 30 [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7) (expert) to quiet the spirit for 1 round, or DC 32 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) to exorcise it

**Routine**

**Source** [Hellcoast Heresies](/Sources.aspx?ID=339) pg. 65 **Complexity** Simple A swirling portal leads to unwholesome places. --- **Stealth** DC 35 (to predict the portal’s dangerous destinations) **Disable** DC 35 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), DC 35 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or DC 35 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master); must have studied Carlina’s notes (see page 66) **Warping Journey** (occult) **Trigger** A creature passes through the doorway; **Effect** The creature is pulled apart and reassembled as they pass through multiple dimensions at once. The creature must attempt a DC 30 Will save and disappears for a number of rounds, reappearing at the end of their turn on the final round. Each round at the beginning of their turn, creatures trapped in the doorway must succeed at a DC 32 Fortitude save against a _cursed metamorphosis_ spell as their bodies are warped and rearranged. A creature can pass through each red-tinged doorway only once. **Critical Success** The creature disappears for 1 round. Additionally, the creature gains 10 temporary Hit Points for 24 hours. These stack with temporary Hit Points gained from other red-tinged doorways and replenish each day at midnight as long as the creature is within 1 mile of Narona.
**Success** The creature disappears for 1 round.
**Failure** The creature disappears for 2 rounds.
**Critical Failure** The creature disappears for 3 rounds. If the creature critically fails its saving throw against a cursed metamorphosis spell, it’s permanently transformed into an amalgamite.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 7" pfs="">[Releasing Laibuson](/Hazards.aspx?ID=794)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Unique" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=723" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [The Dead God's Hand](/Sources.aspx?ID=370) pg. 97

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Five colorful gemstones circle the glass barrier separating the PCs from the quartermaster. Careful manipulation of the gems, which can be turned like knobs, might overload one or more of them.

---

**Stealth**
+20 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 27 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) or DC 30 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) on the circle of gemstones to deactivate one gemstone, extinguishing its glow. A critical success on the check deactivates two gemstones, while a failure triggers the trap and a critical failure not only triggers the trap but resets a previously disabled gemstone. When all five gemstones are deactivated or destroyed, the trap becomes inert, releasing Laibuson.

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 28, **Fort** +18, **Ref** +12

**Gemstone Hardness**
15

**HP**
30 (BT 15)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

</column>

**Customer Feedback** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=647)) **Trigger** A creature damages any of the gemstones or fails a check while attempting to [Disable](/Actions.aspx?ID=2411) one; **Effect** A colorful arc of energy leaps from the glowing gems to surround Laibuson and the triggering creature, causing 4d8 mental damage (DC 25 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Will save) to each. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action; arcane, mental) On its turn, the trap continues to antagonize Laibuson and one randomly determined PC, causing 4d8 mental damage (DC 25 basic Will save) to each. On a critical failure, the creature also becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=94) 1 for the remainder of this vision.

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates if a round passes without any attempts to disable or damage the gems, then resets and can reactivate again immediately.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 15" pfs="">[Rogue Sphere](/Hazards.aspx?ID=392)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #191: The Destiny War](/Sources.aspx?ID=199) pg. 25

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A roving sphere of distorted magic shimmers and floats through the air.

---

**Stealth**
+40 (master; +35 in bright light)

**Disable**
DC 38 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) to cause the magic of the sphere to dissipate harmlessly, or DC 40 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) to cause the sphere to burst and implode safely, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (8th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 34)

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 34, **Fort** +23, **Ref** +29

**Hardness**
25

**HP**
96 (BT 48)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

**Weaknesses**
[force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) 15

</column>

**Magic Drift** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature within 60 feet casts a spell or uses magical effect, or a creature within 60 feet is the target of an active spell that's 5th level or higher, carries a magic item of 10th level or higher, or is the target of an ongoing magical effect created by a creature who's 10th level or higher; **Effect** The sphere flies 30 feet toward the triggering creature. If the sphere would enter a creature's space, it stops moving in that creature's space, then attempts to counter the triggering magic effect (or alternately, the strongest magic effect on the creature), with a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier of +28. A counteracted magic item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. If the target is a creature, or is a creature who's carrying the targeted item, the creature takes 10d6 force damage from this effect (DC 36 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). The rogue sphere then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) The sphere uses its first action to fly 30 feet toward the closest creature currently under the effects of a spell, or it uses both actions to fly 60 feet toward the closest creature if none are within 30 feet. The rogue sphere attempts to enter the target's space. If a rogue sphere shares a creature's space, it uses an action to Magic Drift the target. If the target has no magical effects or carries no magic items, the result of its Fortitude save to resist the force damage caused by Magic Drift is increased by one degree of success.

---
**Reset**
The sphere ceases moving when no creature remains to trigger Magic Drift. It then dissipates after an hour spent with no targets within 60 feet

A counteracted magic item becomes a mundane item of its type for 10 minutes. If the target is a creature, or is a creature who's carrying the targeted item, the creature takes 10d6 force damage from this effect (DC 36 basic Fortitude save). The rogue sphere then rolls initiative. Routine (2 actions) The sphere uses its first action to fly 30 feet toward the closest creature currently under the effects of a spell, or it uses both actions to fly 60 feet toward the closest creature if none are within 30 feet. The rogue sphere attempts to enter the target's space. If a rogue sphere shares a creature's space, it uses an action to Magic Drift the target. If the target has no magical effects or carries no magic items, the result of its Fortitude save to resist the force damage caused by Magic Drift is increased by one degree of success. Reset The sphere ceases moving when no creature remains to trigger Magic Drift. It then dissipates after an hour spent with no targets within 60 feet

This trap appears to be an obvious 10-foot-deep pit with angled walls to prevent easy escape, but the true danger is represented not by the hole in the ground but from a set of loose stones in the ceiling. A knotted rope hangs from a beam above, seemingly to provide an option to swing across the pit, but any weight on the rope pulls down large, heavy boulders stacked far above.

---

**Stealth**
DC 20

**Disable**
DC 20 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to tie off the rope to a more solid support

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Boulders from Above** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A Small or larger creature or equivalent weight pulls on the rope; **Effect** All creatures within the pit or adjacent to the pit take 4d6+10 bludgeoning damage (DC 23 basic Reflex save) from falling rocks dislodged from above.

**Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 49 **Complexity** Simple Rivulets of water begin to run from the circle of stones to gather in a growing puddle at the center. --- **Stealth** DC 20 (trained) **Disable** DC 20 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (expert) to rub out the hidden runes on the ceiling, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (2nd level, [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 18) to counteract the trap **Spherical Deluge** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [water](/Traits.aspx?ID=165)) **Trigger** A creature enters the area south of the ring of stones marked on the map; **Effect** A deluge of water rises up from the ring of stones, then flows forcefully down the passageway to drain into the pit at area **F1b**. Large and smaller creatures in the water's path must attempt a DC 20 Fortitude save. The rushing waters vanish instantly upon striking the pit floor, but do leave everything down there sopping wet. **Critical Success** The creature withstands the force of the rushing waters and is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes 1d10 bludgeoning damage as the rushing waters slam them into a cave wall.
**Failure** The creature is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) by the rushing waters, takes 1d10+6 bludgeoning damage, and is [pushed](/Rules.aspx?ID=451) by the water to the spiky pit trap and triggers the trap.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature can't attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) if they fall into the [spiky pit trap](/Hazards.aspx?ID=424). --- **Reset** The magic rejuvenates over 10 minutes, after which it is recharged and ready to activate again.

**Success** As Critical Success, but the falling trap delivers a glancing blow and 1d6+3 bludgeoning damage to the creature as it stumbles back.

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 67 **Complexity** Complex A phantom conductor appears with a flourish, causing spectral instruments with razor-like strings to appear in the hands of those present. As the conductor gestures for the performance to begin, creatures are compelled to play the instruments. --- **Stealth** +12 (trained) **Disable** DC 18 [Performance](/Skills.aspx?ID=12) to perform so well the conductor releases you from your instrument, banishing it voluntarily; DC 22 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to banish one instrument; or DC 25 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to sabotage one instrument; each instrument must be banished, sabotaged, or destroyed to disable the haunt **Hardness** 10 **HP** 22 per instrument (BT 11) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Conjure Instruments** ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Trigger** A creature approaches within 15 feet; **Effect** The conductor conjures a hazardous spectral instrument into the hands of each sentient creature within 30 feet. Even a creature whose hands are full finds a spectral instrument superimposed over the other items it's carrying. Affected creatures must each attempt a DC 19 Will save. The haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The conjuration fails and no instrument appears in the creature's hands.
**Success** A conjured instrument appears in the creature's hands, but it isn't compelled to play it.
**Failure** A conjured instrument appears in the creature's hands and it's compelled to play it (see routine below). The creature can't willingly put down the instrument while compelled to play.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature needs a critical success on its Performance in order for the conductor to be satisfied and dismiss its instrument. --- **Routine** (1 action; [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) The conductor urges each creature within 30 feet to play the hazardous instrument it holds. Each creature that is compelled to play its instrument does so, and those who succeeded on their save can choose to do so. Playing the instrument, either from the haunt's routine or of a creature's own volition during an attempt to disable the haunt, deals 1d6+3 slashing damage (DC 21 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save), and the creature must attempt a DC 18 Performance check. On a success, the conductor accepts the performance and dismisses that creature's instrument, and on a critical failure, the discordant sound and conductor's jeers deal an additional 1d6+3 sonic damage. --- **Reset** The haunt deactivates when all conjured instruments are destroyed or there has been silence for 1 minute. It resets after 1 hour.

**Source** [Pathfinder #166: Despair on Danger Island](/Sources.aspx?ID=85) pg. 18 **Complexity** Complex Buffeting winds swirl sharp grains of sand about the room. --- **Stealth** +23 (trained) **Disable** DC 38 Religion (expert) to state an [Iroran](/Deities.aspx?ID=10) koan about being complete only upon recognizing one's incompleteness, or DC 41 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (master) to create a ward against future hauntings **Sand Vacuum** **Trigger** A creature attempts to leave the chamber; **Effect** A powerful wind pulls the creature back into the room. The triggering creature must attempt a DC 39 Fortitude save. The haunt can use this reaction any number of times per round, but only once per creature that tries to leave the room. The haunt then rolls initiative, if it hasn't already. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 4" pfs="">[Scholar's Bane](/Hazards.aspx?ID=356)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #187: The Seventh Arch](/Sources.aspx?ID=192) pg. 53

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Illusion magic overwhelms the minds of particularly intelligent creatures, forcing them to relive every intellectual failure and shame they’ve ever sufered.

---

**Stealth**
+14 (trained) to notice magical sensors hidden within four of the carvings’ eyes

**Disable**
DC 22 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to carve out one eye sensor, DC 22 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) (trained) to blank out one's mind (disables trap for self only), or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (2nd level; counteract DC 20) to counteract one eye sensor

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 20, **Fort** +12, **Ref** +8

**Eye Hardness**
6

**Eye HP**
20

</column>

**Reveal Failure** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature with an Intelligence score of 10 or greater enters the room; **Effect** The trap flls the triggering creature's mind with shameful memories. The creature must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or take 2d8+2 mental damage. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(4 actions) The trap uses each action to target a creature in the room with an Intelligence score of 10 or greater. A target must succeed at a DC 22 Will save or take 2d8+2 mental damage. On a critical failure, the creature takes a –10-foot status penalty to Speed for 1 minute as they stagger under the weight of their failures. The trap loses 1 action for each eye sensor disabled or destroyed.

---
**Reset**
The trap can function for 10 rounds, which don’t need to be consecutive, before it must recharge for 24 hours.

**Source** [Pathfinder #215: To Blot Out the Sun](/Sources.aspx?ID=259) pg. 65 **Complexity** Complex The _shadow beacon’s_ operation causes harmful energy to blast out of the base of the device. --- **Stealth** + 18 **Disable** DC 27 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=37) or [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to rig a dispersal system, or DC 27 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (master) to safely vent the magical energy; four total successes in any combination to disable **Priming** ([cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=555), [shadow](/Traits.aspx?ID=693)) **Trigger** Nizca and Deg activate the shadow beacon; **Effect** The shadow beacon sparks to life. The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) The shadow beacon fires shadows into the sky, discharging excess energy out of the device’s lower half. The trap deals 4d6 cold and 4d6 void damage to all non-shadow creatures in a 60-foot [emanation](/Rules.aspx?ID=2387) from the base of the device (DC 26 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=2297) Fortitude save). For each successful check to disable the trap, the cold and void damage dealt by the trap on subsequent rounds are both reduced by 1d6 damage. A creature that fails their save is pushed back 10 feet (15 feet on a critical failure).

**Special** Disabling the shadow discharge does not disable the shadow beacon.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #191: The Destiny War](/Sources.aspx?ID=199) pg. 35 **Complexity** Complex Shifting illusions disorient, entrap, and agonize those who attempt to pass through the shadowy maze. --- **Stealth** +32 (master) to realize the water within the dome poses a supernatural threat **Disable** DC 42 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to decouple faint strands of shadow essence from the magical matrix that holds the maze together, DC 45 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) to shunt the shadowy energy back into the [Shadow Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=11) and render the maze inert, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (8th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 35) to counteract the shadow maze **Disorient** ([illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) **Trigger** A creature enters the 20-foot-wide interior of the shadow maze, either from area **C2** or **C4**, or through a hole smashed in the dome; **Effect** Reality appears to shift around the creature, who perceives a sudden transformation in the surrounding terrain into a vast maze of underwater alleys and crumbling ruins. The creature must attempt a DC 37 Will save, and the shadow maze then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature sees through the illusions and can move freely through squares within the shadow maze's effect. It's temporarily immune to the effects of the trap's routine for 1 minute.
**Success** The creature understands that what it's experiencing is an illusion, but it isn't immune to the effects of the trap's routine.
**Failure** The creature believes it has stepped into a vast maze. To those observing the creature outside of the shadow maze, the creature remains motionless. The creature becomes [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round, during which time all of its speeds are reduced to 5 feet.
**Critical Failure** The creature not only believes it has entered a vast maze, but is overwhelmed with the sensation of being hopelessly lost. The creature is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=24) until the end of its next turn. --- **Routine** (1 action; [illusion](/Traits.aspx?ID=92), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)) The shadow maze shifts and adjusts its appearance, affecting all creatures currently located within its area. Any creatures in the area at this time must attempt a DC 37 Will save.
**Critical Success** The creature sees through the illusions and can act normally.
**Success** The creature treats all squares within the trap's area as difficult terrain, and the trap fills the creature's mind with sensations and false memories that it has been wandering these alleys for nearly an hour. The creature takes 5d6 mental damage from the perceived strain of navigating the alien flooded alleys.
**Failure** As success, but the creature believes it has been wandering the alleys for several hours. It becomes [slowed 2](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for 1 round and takes 10d6 mental damage from the perceived strain.
**Critical Failure** The creature believes it has been hopelessly lost in the alleys of the shadow maze for days, and it is incapacitated for 1 round and takes 20d6 mental damage from the perceived strain. --- **Reset** If disarmed, the trap resets in 1 hour as long as the two crystals in area **C5** still function.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 10" pfs="">[Shadow Roil](/Hazards.aspx?ID=510)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=683" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Shadow" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=693" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #202: Severed at the Root](/Sources.aspx?ID=242) pg. 53

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A cyclone of living shadows and planar magic surges around the area, attracted to living creatures.

---

**Stealth**
+15 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 32 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) (expert) to weaken the tornado; three successes in any combination are required to disable the trap.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Touch Down** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** Two or more living creatures enter the area; **Effect** A spiraling column of shadows and crackling planar magic gathers 20 feet away, becoming a whirling cyclone of darkness 15 feet wide and 100 feet tall. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The cyclone uses 3 actions to move, traveling up to 30 feet with each action and dealing 2d12+13 slashing damage to each creature in its path (DC 33 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). A creature needs to attempt only one save during the cyclone's movement, even if the cyclone moves over its space more than once. On a critical failure, a creature is swept up into the cyclone, becoming [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=77) ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=2296) DC 33). A creature grabbed by the cyclone moves along with the cyclone and takes 1d12+7 additional slashing damage at the beginning of its turn, and it must attempt the [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against the cyclone on the cyclone's turn, no matter where the cyclone moves. A creature that successfully Escapes from the cyclone [falls](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) from a height of 1d20 × 5 feet.

---
**Reset**
The cyclone disperses after 1 minute and resets after 1 day.

**Source** [Pathfinder #200: Seven Dooms for Sandpoint](/Sources.aspx?ID=229) pg. 138 **Complexity** Complex Swirling shadows that behave like animated pools of ink splash and slither up against the limbs of those who tread too far into this chamber. --- **Stealth** +19 (master) **Disable** Three DC 33 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=35) or [Occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=662) checks to redirect the negative energy back in on itself and disrupt the hazard's source of power, a DC 36 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) check to offer prayers to sever the sacred link to Kabriri, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (6th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 29) to render the hazard inert for 10 minutes **Sap Strength** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=579), [incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=631), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** A creature moves into the room beyond the northern stairs; **Effect** Shadowy tendrils wisp up from the darkness below to brush against the triggering creature's body. The creature must attempt a DC 30 Fortitude save or their strength is sapped from their body. The hazard then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature’s speeds are reduced by 10 feet for 1 round.
**Failure** As success, but the creature also falls [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88).
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the creature also becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=85). It can attempt a new save at the end of each of its turns, and the DC cumulatively decreases by 1 on each such save. --- **Routine** 1 action) The shadows writhing on the floor extrude a storm of inky tentacles of smoke and darkness that whip and writhe throughout the room, filling the air with unsettling sounds of agonizing cries and shrieks. All creatures in area **J3a** take 8d6 negative damage (DC 30 basic Fortitude save). --- **Reset** The hazard settles back down 1 round after all creatures leave the room and can trigger again at the start of the next round.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Kingmaker Companion Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=151) pg. 90 **Complexity** Simple The statue begins to weep, its tears running in rivulets down into the surrounding pool, filling all nearby with overwhelming shame and grief. --- **Stealth** DC 33 (master) to notice tears beginning to run from the statue’s eyes **Disable** DC 29 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) to offer prayers to Shelyn (a worshipper of Shelyn gains a +2 circumstance bonus to this check), or DC 33 [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6) (expert) to offer condolences and comforts to the haunt **Hope or Despair** **Trigger** A Small or larger creature enters the pool or touches the statue; **Effect** The waters of the pool and the statue become infused with divine power. The triggering creature and all other creatures within 20 feet of that creature must attempt a DC 30 Will save. If the save is attempted by a worshipper of Shelyn, the result is automatically improved one degree. **Critical Success** Shelyn sees in the creature a chance to bring the shrine back to glory, and instead of filling them with despair, the haunt fills them with hope. In addition to being filled with an urge to defeat the evil that has infested the shrine, the creature has the urge to restore the shrine. Exact details as to the nature of the evil infesting the shrine aren't apparent other than to alert the character that there's certainly something dire within the shrine's walls. The creature need not act on these urges, but as long as they pursue either goal, they gain a +1 status bonus to all checks while remaining in the shrine's area. The GM determines whether or not a check counts toward this goal (at the very least, all combat checks made against foes in the rest of the adventure count).
**Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Failure** Feelings of sadness and despair well up in the creature's mind. For the next hour, the creature takes a –1 penalty to all saving throws against mental effects; this penalty increases to a –2 penalty against emotion mental effects. This effect has the [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38) trait.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the effects persist as long as the green hag Tulvak remains in control of the shrine.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 2" pfs="">[Shrinking Hall](/Hazards.aspx?ID=183)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 123

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

This hallway is designed to shrink as creatures traverse it, making access to the door at the hall's end impossible.

---

**Stealth**
DC 18

**Disable**
DC 21 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to jam the scales built into the floor

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Shrink** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** 100 pounds of weight or more is placed on the hallway's floor; **Effect** The hall's last 40 feet of walls angle inward, causing the hall to shrink and contract down, reaching 6 inches in height and width at the hall's far end and completely blocking access to the hall's exit door for anything but a Tiny creature [Squeezing](/Actions.aspx?ID=31).

---
**Reset**
After 10 minutes without weight being placed on this hall's floor, this trap resets, returning the hall to its original size.

<traits>
<trait label="Mechanical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=105" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 122

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

Four pressure plates along this mirrored hall rotate vertically when stepped on, sending a creature on the pressure plate tipping into an adjacent featureless room while simultaneously replacing the pressure plate and walls in the hall. Each pressure plate dumps creatures into a different room.

---

**Stealth**
DC 15

**Disable**
DC 12 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) to deactivate one pressure plate

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 18, **Fort** +2, **Ref** +5

**Hardness**
4

**HP**
12 (BT 6)

**Immunities**
object immunities

</column>

**Flip** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature steps on a pressure plate; **Effect** The floor and adjoining wall rotate up and over on a central axle, tipping the triggering creature into an adjacent featureless room and simultaneously replacing the pressure plate and wall with another set on the same axle. The triggering creature is pushed into an adjoining room, takes 1d8 bludgeoning damage, and lands [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31). A creature who succeeds at a DC 19 Reflex save takes no damage and rolls out of the way of the trap, returning to the space they were in before stepping on the pressure plate.

---
**Reset**
automatic

**Source** [Pathfinder #164: Hands of the Devil](/Sources.aspx?ID=75) pg. 21 **Complexity** Complex Six long blades, hidden in grooves in the walls and floor, zigzag through different parts of this hallway when any pressure plate in the hallway intersection is depressed; there are so many plates it’s impossible to avoid them when moving through the room. The blades retreat into the floor and move through the hidden grooves before swinging out from the wall again in a different location. --- **Stealth** DC +18 (expert) **Disable** DC 26 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (expert) to disable each blade, or utter the magical passphrase (which only Chafkhem knows) to deactivate the trap for 10 minutes **AC** 27, **Fort** +19, **Ref** +13 **Scythe Blade Hardness** 16 **Scythe Blade HP** 30 (BT 15) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Dicing Scythes** **Trigger** A creature steps in the 15-footby- 25-foot area where the branching hallways connect; Effect The trap uses Scythe Shuffle; each blade makes a scythe Strike against each creature in its region, then it uses Scythe Shuffle again. The trap then rolls for initiative.
Scythe Shuffle The blades travel erratically throughout the hallway’s branches, out of sight under the floors or behind the walls. fields.markdown:
**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 69 **Complexity** Complex A formless spirit drains life from the living, becoming progressively visible as its victims weaken. --- **Stealth** +40 (trained) **Disable** DC 48 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (expert) to weaken the spirit; four total successes are required to disable the haunt **Sudden Siphon** ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118)) **Trigger** A living creature passes within 15 feet of the spirit; **Effect** The invisible spirit latches onto the life essence of the living, dealing 4d10+20 negative damage to all living creatures within 60 feet (DC 41 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Fortitude save). The haunt then rolls initiative. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and increases its [drained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) value by 1, to a maximum of drained 4.
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and increases its drained value by 2, to a maximum of drained 4. If the creature was already drained 4, it dies. --- **Routine** (1 action; [death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117), [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118)) The spirit inhales, siphoning the souls of the living and becoming more visible. Each creature within 60 feet takes 4d10+20 negative damage, with a DC 41 Fortitude save. If no creatures are within the area, the haunt moves up to 120 feet into the largest concentration of living creatures and then inhales. --- **Reset** After 1 minute, the spirit is satiated, and the haunt deactivates as it returns to a resting state. Over the course of 1 hour, the spirit's siphoned life energy disperses and the haunt resets.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #220: Crypt of Runes](/Sources.aspx?ID=284) pg. 39 **Complexity** Complex A supernatural exhaustion fills creatures who climb the stairs. --- **Stealth** +35 (master) **Disable** DC 45 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (legendary) to wedge crumbling stones into cracks to jam the collapsing stairs, DC 48 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to deface the [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=79) magical runes that power the trap; or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (9th rank, [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=3280) DC 36) to counteract a rune; three total successes are required to disable the trap **Collapse** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) **Trigger** A creature inspects the wall at the top of the stairs or begins to descend the stairs after reaching the top; **Effect** The floor at the bottom of the stairwell disappears, revealing a seemingly bottomless pit. Meanwhile, the stairwell begins to collapse, starting from the top and working its way down. Any PC standing on the lower few steps falls into the pit unless they Grab the Edge with a successful DC 40 Reflex save. The trap then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (2 actions) The haunt uses Leaden Limbs once, then Crumbling Stairs once. **Leaden Limbs** ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=534)) The trap drains vigor from creatures in the stairwell, making their limbs feel as heavy as lead. Each creature in the area must attempt a DC 40 Fortitude saving throw with the following results. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 until the end of their next turn.
**Failure** The creature’s [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) condition value increases by 1, to a maximum of clumsy 4. The creature is slowed 1 as long as they remain clumsy. The clumsy condition ends as soon as the creature exits the stairwell.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the value increases by 2, and the creature is slowed 2. **Crumbling Stairs** A stretch of stairs crumbles, dropping into the void at the bottom of the stairwell. The first time the trap takes this action, the upper third of the stairwell collapses. The second time, the middle third collapses. The third time, the entire stairwell collapses. A creature on a collapsing section of stairs can try to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=2313) with a DC 40 Reflex save to avoid falling into the void. Flying creatures avoid the fall automatically but might tumble into the void anyway if their [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) condition prevents them from taking the Fly action on their turn. Though it appears to stretch forever, the void at the bottom of the stairwell functions as a portal to the Crypt of Sloth. Creatures who plummet into the void experience a fall that seems to take hours, but are eventually deposited in the middle of area **B10**, taking 80 bludgeoning damage from the fall. --- **Reset** The trap continues taking Leaden Limbs actions (and the void at the bottom of the stairwell remains open) for as long as creatures remain in the area. Once no creatures remain, the stairwell rebuilds itself, the void closes, and the trap resets.

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=591" />
<trait label="Poison" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=669" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Tailors and Traitors](/Sources.aspx?ID=344) pg. 148

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Smoke billows out from the chimney and fills the room.

---

**Stealth**
+0

**Disable**
DC 40 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) (expert) to pull the blockage from the chimney, DC 46 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (master) to clear the chimney by removing a crucial object and cause everything to fall out, or _create water_ (or similar effect) to extinguish the fire

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Choking Smoke** <actions string="Reaction" /> (inhaled, poison) **Trigger** A creature other than Ivirno enters area **A6**; **Effect** Smoke fills the room, concealing all creatures within area **A6**. All creatures in the area other than Ivirno take 11d6 poison damage (DC 43 basic Fortitude save), then the smoking chimney rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action; inhaled, poison) The smoking chimney billows out smoke. If the door from area **A6** is open, the smoke expands 5 feet into the corridor. All creatures in the smoke take 11d6 poison damage (DC 43 basic Fortitude save). On a failure, the target becomes [sickened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=91) 1 for 1 round.

---
**Reset**
The smoking chimney resets when 10 Bulk of objects are placed in it.

1 hour, as the vine grows a new set of barbs

**Source** [Pathfinder #189: Dreamers of the Nameless Spires](/Sources.aspx?ID=195) pg. 13 **Complexity** Simple Several hidden nozzles spray colorless sleeping gas into the seating area. --- **Stealth** DC 28 (expert) **Disable** DC 28 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (expert) to crimp shut the primary feeding tube for the gas, or DC 31 Perception (expert) to discover the hidden bypass switch next to the door to area **A3** that shuts the trap off **Gas Spray** ([incapacitation](/Traits.aspx?ID=93), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), [sleep](/Traits.aspx?ID=145)) **Trigger** Pressure is applied to any of the steps in the middle of the seating area, or applied to the manual trigger on the stage. This manual trigger can activate the trap even if its hidden bypass switch is engaged; **Effect** Sleeping gas is silently sprayed into the seating area. All creatures in the area must roll a DC 26 Will save to resist its effects. The gas persists in the area for 3 rounds before becoming inert. Any creature who ends their turn in this area during these 3 rounds must attempt a new DC 26 Will save. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected and realizes that the area has been gassed.
**Success** The creature is unaffected but doesn't notice the gas.
**Failure** The creature feels a bit drowsy and lethargic, and becomes [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) for 1 minute. If the creature is already fatigued, it instead falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38). If it's still unconscious after 1 minute, it wakes up automatically.
**Critical Failure** The creature falls unconscious. If it's still unconscious after 1 hour, it wakes up automatically.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #186: Ghost King's Rage](/Sources.aspx?ID=189) pg. 22

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

Four steel pillars emit pulsing energy to slow souls' processes.

---

**Stealth**
+33 (master)

**Disable**
DC 43 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (master) to reweave the magic within each pillar, DC 46 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to disable each pillar, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (8th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 43) to counteract each pillar

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 40, **Fort** +32, **Ref** +26

**Pillar Hardness**
29

**Pillar HP**
114 (BT 57)

**Immunities**
critical hits, object immunities, precision damage

</column>

**Pulse** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48)) **Trigger** A soul or creature with a soul enters the area; **Effect** The steel pillars activate with an audible hum that resonates with spirits. Each non-[psychopomp](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=83) creature with a soul is [stunned 3](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36) unless they succeed at a DC 43 Will save. The trap then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(4 actions) This trap loses 1 action each turn for each disabled pillar. Each pillar uses 1 action to emit a 30-foot-radius burst of inhibiting energy that slows souls. Each non-psychopomp creature with a soul in the area is [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) unless they succeed at a DC 43 Fortitude save.

---
**Reset**
The trap deactivates and resets if 1 minute passes without any souls in the area.

The reflection in the mirror subtly twists and distorts, its expression taking on an unnerving sneer of malice.

---

**Stealth**
DC 26 (expert)

50 (BT 25)

</column>

**Spectral Impale** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A living creature approaches within 15 feet of the mirror, and the mirror is lit with dim or brighter light; **Effect** Shadowy barbs impale the body of the reflected creature as the haunt makes a shadow barbs Strike.

 **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> shadow barbs +19, **Damage** 4d8+9 negative plus sap vitality 

**Sap Vitality** A creature hit by the reflection’s shadow barbs must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save as the haunt tries to draw a portion of its vital essence into the mirror. The target is [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10) on a failed saving throw, or drained 2 on a critical failure.

---
**Reset**
The haunt re-forms after 1 minute, manifesting in any mirror within its infused area (see Special below). 

**Special** Spectral reflections often infuse entire buildings, manifesting in any sufficiently large mirror. The example Hit Points and Hardness given represent a typical mirror reinforced by the haunt; at your discretion, the haunt might appear in reflective surfaces that are harder to destroy. Defeating a manifestation through damage destroys the surface, preventing the haunt from using it again. If this haunt appears in an area with many mirrors, consider giving PCs double or even triple the XP for a typical simple hazard.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 5" pfs="">[Spectral Reflection](/Hazards.aspx?ID=484)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 104

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

The reflection in the mirror subtly twists and distorts, its expression taking on an unnerving sneer of malice.

---

**Stealth**
DC 26 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 23 [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=46) (trained) to exorcise the spirit, or DC 23 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=50) (trained) to quickly cover the mirror

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 19, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +10

**Hardness**
13

**HP**
50 (BT 25)

**Immunities**
[critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2190), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage

</column>

**Spectral Impale** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A living creature approaches within 15 feet of the mirror, and the mirror is lit with [dim](/Rules.aspx?ID=2403) or brighter [light](/Rules.aspx?ID=2401); **Effect** Shadowy barbs impale the body of the reflected creature as the haunt makes a shadow barbs [Strike](/Actions.aspx?ID=2306). 

**Melee** shadow barbs +19, **Damage** 4d8+9 [void](/Traits.aspx?ID=510) plus sap vitality 

**Sap Vitality** A creature hit by the reflection’s shadow barbs must attempt a DC 22 Fortitude save as the haunt tries to draw a portion of its vital essence into the mirror. The target is [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=68) on a failed saving throw, or drained 2 on a critical failure.

---
**Reset**
The haunt re-forms after 1 minute, manifesting in any mirror within its infused area (see Special Below). 

**Special** Spectral reflections often infuse entire buildings, manifesting in any sufficiently large mirror. The example Hit Points and Hardness given represent a typical mirror reinforced by the haunt; at your discretion, the haunt might appear in reflective surfaces that are harder to destroy. Defeating a manifestation through damage destroys the surface, preventing the haunt from using it again. If this haunt appears in an area with many mirrors, consider giving PCs double or even triple the XP for a typical simple hazard.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 1" pfs="">[Spell Pitchers](/Hazards.aspx?ID=306)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Environmental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=62" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Impossible Lands](/Sources.aspx?ID=146) pg. 232

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A large pitcher plant occupying a 5-foot space sits seemingly dormant with its dull petals open.

---

**Stealth**
DC 20 (trained) to recognize the plant among others

**Disable**
DC 15 [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2) (trained) to safely trigger the plant's reflexes, causing it to close and become dormant for one day, or DC 17 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) (trained) to carefully coax the pitcher into quiescence

<column gap="tiny">

**AC** 16, **Fort** +11, **Ref** +5

**HP**
40 (BT 20)

**Immunities**
[mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106)

**Weaknesses**
slashing 10

</column>

**Devour Magic** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A spell's direct line of effect passes within a 5-foot-radius of the plant; **Effect** The pitcher attempts to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the spell (counteract level 1, counteract modifier +10). On a success, the pitcher immediately consumes the spell as it passes over the plant.

---
**Reset**
Once the pitcher has eaten a spell, its petals turn dark pink and green before it closes. It goes dormant for one day per spell level of the spell consumed. Once the pitcher finishes digesting, it opens again and slowly wilts. A second pitcher branches into an adjacent square when the first pitcher opens again.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 11" pfs="">[Spider Summoning Rune](/Hazards.aspx?ID=101)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=158" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 66

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

An invisible rune on the floor summons a [goliath spider](/Monsters.aspx?ID=388) when disturbed by someone who isn't wearing [Norgorber's](/Deities.aspx?ID=13) [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41).

---

**Stealth**
+24 (master)

**Disable**
DC 34 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (master) to erase the rune or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (6th level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 36) to dispel the rune.

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Summon Animal** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [summon](/Traits.aspx?ID=154)) **Trigger** A creature that isn't wearing a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of [Norgorber](/Deities.aspx?ID=13) enters the area above the rune; **Effect** The trap summons a [goliath spider](/Monsters.aspx?ID=388). The goliath spider rolls initiative and remains for 2d6 rounds, after which the spell ends and the spider disappears. The spider also disappears if someone disables the trap before the duration expires. Unlike most summoned creatures, the goliath spider can use 3 actions each round and can use reactions.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets after 24 hours.

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Rusthenge](/Sources.aspx?ID=215) pg. 49

**Complexity** Simple

</column>

A piece of hide covered with a layer of dirt and gravel is suspended over a 20-foot pit filled with spikes.

---

**Stealth**
DC 18 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 18 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to manually trigger the trap without falling in, or DC 25 Thievery (trained) to secure the hide so the trap doesn't activate

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Pitfall** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature or other large weight (such as the rushing waters of the [previous trap](/Hazards.aspx?ID=423)) moves onto the gravel-covered hide; **Effect** The triggering creature or object falls in and takes [falling damage](/Rules.aspx?ID=402) (10 bludgeoning damage) and is targeted by a spike's Strike. A falling creature can attempt to [Grab an Edge](/Actions.aspx?ID=95) with a DC 20 Reflex save (this becomes a DC 22 Reflex save if rushing waters are pouring into the pit). **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> spike +14, **Damage** 4d8 piercing

---
**Reset**
Creatures can still fall into the trap, but the hide that covers it must be reset manually (a 10-minute activity) for the trap to become hidden again.

<title level="1" right="Hazard 9" pfs="">[Spirit Cyclone](/Hazards.aspx?ID=154)</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Haunt" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=88" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 68

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A cyclone of angry spirits surges around the area.

---

**Stealth**
+20 (expert)

**Disable**
DC 30 [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) (trained) to weaken the haunt; three total successes in any combination are required to disable the haunt

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Gather Spirits** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** Two or more creatures enter the area; **Effect** A spiraling column of spirits gather, becoming a whirling cyclone of souls 10 feet wide and 60 feet tall. The haunt then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(3 actions) The spirit cyclone uses 3 actions to move, traveling up to 30 feet with each action and dealing 2d10+13 negative damage to each creature in its path (DC 32 [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save). A creature needs to attempt only one save during the cyclone's movement, even if the cyclone moves over its space more than once. On a critical failure, a creature is swept up into the cyclone, becoming [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) ([Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) DC 32). A creature grabbed by the cyclone moves along with the cyclone and takes 1d10+6 additional negative damage at their beginning of its turn, and it must attempt a Reflex save against the cyclone on the cyclone's turn, no matter where the cyclone moves. A creature that successfully Escapes from the cyclone falls from a height of 1d12 × 5 feet.

---
**Reset**
The spirit cyclone disperses after 1 minute and resets after 1 day.

**Source** [Sweet Tooth](/Sources.aspx?ID=332) pg. 86 **Complexity** Complex A massive bronze cauldron of molten candy bubbles on the stove, spraying sticky-sweet hot caramel in all directions. --- **Stealth** +10 **Disable** Breaking the pot disables it as soon as its rupture reaction is resolved. **AC** 17, **Fort** +9 **Hardness** 5 **HP** 40 (BT 20) **Immunities** [critical hits](/Rules.aspx?ID=2314), [object immunities](/Rules.aspx?ID=2161), precision damage **Bubble Bubble** (occult) **Trigger** Larmine rolls initiative; **Effect** With a wave of her hand, Larmine instantly brings her candy pot to a violent boil. The pot blows its top and targets all creatures hostile to Larmine within 20 feet of it, dealing 2d8 fire damage with a DC 16 basic Reflex save. On a critical failure, the targeted creature also takes 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) as the hot candy sticks to their exposed skin. The spitting hot candy pot then rolls initiative. **Rupture** [reaction] **Trigger** The spitting hot candy pot Breaks; **Effect** The pot splits open, spilling its remaining contents in a 15-foot cone that deals 2d12 fire damage with a DC 20 Reflex save. The area covered by this reaction lingers as [difficult terrain](/Rules.aspx?ID=2366) for the rest of the encounter. **Critical Success** The creature is unaffected.
**Success** The creature takes half damage.
**Failure** The creature takes full damage and becomes tangled in the sticky mess of hot candy, which imposes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds until it leaves the area of the rupture’s effect. Until the creature leaves the area of effect, it also takes 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86).
**Critical Failure** The creature takes double damage and is [immobilized](/Conditions.aspx?ID=81) (DC 18 to Escape), after which it takes a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds and 1d4 persistent fire damage as Failure. --- **Routine** (2 actions) On each of the pot’s actions, it targets one creature hostile against Larmine within 30 feet of the pot, spitting a glob of hot molten candy that deals 1d8+4 fire damage; the target creature must attempt a DC 16 Reflex save. **Critical Success** The target is unaffected.
**Success** The target takes half damage.
**Failure** The target takes full damage and is [slowed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=92) 1 as the sticky molten candy glues them to the floor.
**Critical Failure** The target takes double damage, is slowed 2, and takes 1d4 [persistent fire damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=86) as the hot candy sticks to their exposed skin.

<traits>
<trait label="Complex" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=30" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=644" />
<trait label="Trap" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=715" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Devils of Chitterwood](/Sources.aspx?ID=310) pg. 55

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A large patch of moss ripples like the surface of a pond as spears of green plant matter jut outward.

---

**Stealth**
+7 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 17 [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=43) or [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=44) twice to cut off the unstable connection to the [Plane of Wood](/Planes.aspx?ID=25), or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1493) (2nd rank; counteract DC 16) to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) the planar magic

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Planar Ripple** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)) **Trigger** Two or more non-plant creatures step onto the moss pond; **Effect** The moss pond ripples oddly as its connection to the Plane of Wood intensifies. Each creature on the pond must succeed at a DC 17 Reflex save or be knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=88). A creature who critically fails the save also takes 1d6 bludgeoning damage from the fall. The pond then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(2 actions) For each action, the moss pond makes a spore spear Strike against a random non-plant creature on or within 10 feet of the moss pond. **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> spore spear +9 ([reach](/Traits.aspx?ID=684) 10 feet, [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=669), [wood](/Traits.aspx?ID=508)); **Damage** 1d6+1 piercing plus 1d4 poison; no multiple attack penalty

---
**Reset**
If the trap isn’t disabled, it becomes dormant for 10 minutes if there are no creatures on or within 10 feet of the moss patch at the start of its turn.

A fire engulfs a 5-foot-by-5-foot area, then spreads on each of its turns.

---

**Stealth**
–10; initiative modifier is +5

**Disable**
DC 17 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) to splash the barrels of gall ink on the fire or DC 15 [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) to smother the flames

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Spreading Flames** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** A creature enters the printing house; **Effect** The flames swell at the influx of air and deal 1d6 fire damage (DC 17 basic Reflex save). The fire then rolls initiative.

---
**Routine**
(1 action) On its turn, the fire spreads into a number of additional squares equal to half the number of squares the fire currently occupies, with a minimum of 1 square. You determine the squares the fire spreads into—typically those with the most flammable materials. Any creature that ends its turn next to the flames takes 1d6 fire damage, and any creature within the flames takes 4d6 fire damage. Both of these have a DC 17 basic Reflex save. A creature can take damage from flames only once per round.

**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 33 **Complexity** Simple A nozzle attached to a pressure sensor under the flagstone path sprays thick wads of smelly sap. --- **Stealth** DC 18 (trained) **Disable** DC 15 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to clog the nozzle or DC 14 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) (trained) to redirect the stream away from the path; the Athletics check can be made at a distance with a thrown object, but a critical failure triggers the trap's Sudden Spray. **AC** 13, **Fort** +8, **Ref** +5 **Nozzle Hardness** 10 **Nozzle HP** 30 (BT 15) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Sudden Spray** **Trigger** A creature or object weighing at least 50 pounds is placed on one of the flagstones north of the gate (marked “T” on the map on page 32); **Effect** Pressurized sap sprays from the nozzle, coating everything in a 15-foot cone. Creatures in the area that fail a DC 20 Reflex save become affected by stink sap.
**Stink Sap** ([aura](/Traits.aspx?ID=206), [olfactory](/Traits.aspx?ID=246)) 5 feet. Creatures and their equipment coated in the sap smell horrible. Creatures in the aura must attempt a DC 16 Fortitude save. On a failure, the creature is [sickened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=34), and on a critical failure, the creature is also [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). While within the aura, the creature takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saves to recover from the sickened condition. A creature that succeeds at its save is immune to stink sap for 1 minute. Creatures don't save against this effect in [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66) mode and don't become temporarily immune, but creatures with stink sap on them must roll against their own aura when they roll initiative in encounter mode. The sap dissipates after 10 hours; spending 10 minutes scrubbing the sap off with soap and water reduces the duration by 1 hour. --- **Reset** 1 minute. The trap resets automatically twice before the supply of stink sap is exhausted.

All creatures on the ship that aren’t lashed to it are moved 10 feet in that direction and must attempt a DC 30 Reflex save or Sailing Lore check as the waves pummel them. Critical Success The creature takes no damage and can avoid being moved 10 feet if it wishes. Success The creature takes no damage. Failure The creature is off-guard and takes 1d12+15 bludgeoning damage. Critical Failure The creature is prone and takes 2d12+15 bludgeoning damage.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #178: Punks in a Powderkeg](/Sources.aspx?ID=119) pg. 62 **Complexity** Complex A mechanical sensor in the desk drawer releases a counterweight in the wall, which slams the door shut and opens the sleeping gas tank under the bed, allowing gas to fill the air-tight room with a hissing sound. --- **Stealth** +10 (Expert) **Disable** DC 26 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (Trained) to disconnect the wire to the counterweight, preventing it from falling, or DC 20 [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4) ([Alchemical Crafting](/Feats.aspx?ID=752)) to create a counteragent to the sleeping gas **AC** 10, **Fort** +15, **Ref** +9 **Hardness** 10 **HP** 40 (BT 2) **Immunities** critical hits, object immunities, precision damage **Slam Door** **Trigger** A creature opens the desk drawer without holding the release button under the desk; **Effect** The wooden door to the room slams shut and locks, and the trap rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) Each round on its initiative count, the trap pumps more sleeping gas into the room. Any breathing creature in the room is exposed to the toxin. If a creature acts before the trap on the first round, it has the option of holding its breath to postpone breathing in the poison—holding one's breath after the trap's first action has no effect, since the air in the creature's lungs is already tainted. The trap functions for 1 minute before all the gas is expended, after which it rapidly decays over the next minute. Opening the door to an adjacent room cuts the remaining time it takes for the gas to decay in half but exposes creatures in that room as well.
**Sleeping Gas** ([inhaled](/Traits.aspx?ID=96), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126)) **Saving Throw** DC 22 Fortitude; **Maximum Duration** 4 hours; **Stage 1** slowed 1 (1 round); **Stage 2** [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) with no Perception check to wake up (1 round); **Stage 3** unconscious with no Perception check to wake up (1 hour) --- **Reset** The gas must be manually reloaded.

**Stealth**
+26 (expert) to hear the echoed shouts of panicked [xulgaths](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=102)

[death](/Traits.aspx?ID=40) effects, [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [poison](/Traits.aspx?ID=126), precision, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38)

all damage 20 (except [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72), [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75), [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297), or [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128))

---
**Routine**
(4 actions) Each active spirit chooses a living non-wendigo creature within 120 feet and attempts to devour it, targeting different creatures if possible. Each calmed spirit reduces the hazard's actions by 1.

 **Melee** <actions string="Single Action" /> ghostly bite +32 ([magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103)), **Damage** 3d6+5 negative

---
**Reset**
The haunt is deactivated and resets 1 minute after all non-wendigo creatures leave the area.

**Source** [Core Rulebook](/Sources.aspx?ID=1) pg. 526

**Complexity** Complex

</column>

A cloud of invisible magical sensors in a 10-foot radius surrounds an invisible wall or floor rune the size of the creature to be summoned.

---

**Stealth**
+7 (trained)

**Disable**
[Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) DC 15 to approach without triggering the trap followed by [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) DC 17 (trained) to erase the rune, or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (1st level; counteract DC 15) to counteract the rune

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Summon Monster** <actions string="Reaction" /> (arcane, conjuration, summon); **Trigger** A creature enters the cloud of magical sensors. **Effect** This trap summons a specific level 1 creature, determined when the trap is created. The creature rolls initiative and remains for 2d6 rounds, after which the spell ends and the creature disappears. The creature also disappears if someone disables the trap before the duration expires. The summoned creature can use 3 actions each round and can use reactions, unlike most summoned creatures.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets each day at dawn

<title level="3">Upgraded Summoning Runes</title> You can make a summoning rune of nearly any level. It summons a creature of a level equal to the trap’s level. Use Table 10–5: DCs by Level on page 503 to determine the Thievery DC and spell DC, using the trap’s level and applying a hard adjustment (+2). The Stealth modifier for the trap is equal to this number – 10. Stronger summoning runes usually require expert proficiency or better in Perception to find, and they might require a higher proficiency rank in Thievery to disable.

Stealth +12 (trained) Disable DC 22 Acrobatics (trained) to approach without triggering the trap, followed by DC 22 Thievery (trained) to erase the rune or dispel magic (3rd level; counteract DC 20) to counteract the rune Summon Elementals Reaction (arcane, conjuration, summon) Trigger A living creature enters the room; Effect Two rounds after a creature enters the room, the room's door slams shut and locks (two DC 20 Thievery checks to pick), and two cinder rat fire elementals emerge from the floor. <column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #157: Devil at the Dreaming Palace](/Sources.aspx?ID=45) pg. 51, [GM Core](/Sources.aspx?ID=218) pg. 108

**Complexity** Complex

A summoning circle inlaid into the room's floor detects living creatures and summons a violent [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30).

---

**Stealth**
+11 (trained)

**Disable**
DC 18 Perception to notice the trap's magic and avoid stepping on the floor outside the circle, followed by DC 21 [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) (trained) to break the circle or [_dispel magic_](/Spells.aspx?ID=78) (3rd level; [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC 23) to counteract the rune

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

**Summon Devil** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([arcane](/Traits.aspx?ID=11), [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33), summon) **Trigger** A living creature steps on any part of the floor not enclosed by the summoning circle; **Effect** One round after a creature touches the triggering area, the door to the room slams shut and locks (two DC 20 Thievery checks to pick) and a [barbazu](/Monsters.aspx?ID=110) devil appears in the summoning circle. The devil rolls initiative and remains for 3d6 rounds, after which the spell ends and the devil disappears. The devil also disappears if someone disables the trap before the duration expires. The summoned devil can use 3 actions each round and can use reactions, unlike most [summoned](/Traits.aspx?ID=154) creatures.

---
**Reset**
The trap resets each day at dawn.

fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #218: Titanbane ](/Sources.aspx?ID=274) pg. 54 **Complexity** Complex Feeling the presence of creatures on its backside, the Granite Ox swishes its stone tail to swat them away.
**Escaping** The PCs overcome this hazard by moving out of the area that the Ox’s tail can reach. A PC escapes (and is not subject to tail Strikes) by ascending the Ox’s sloped back, traveling a distance based on the result of the PC’s Reflex save from the Shaken Loose hazard. PCs can [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=2374) up the Ox’s back with a successful DC 24 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=36) check or—by finding and scrambling up improvised paths—a DC 26 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34), [Perception](/Rules.aspx?ID=2298), or [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=49) check. With a successful DC 20 Acrobatics check, a flying PC can ascend half their fly Speed (or their full Speed on a critical success). PCs can attempt to Disable the hazard whether or not they’re in range of the tail. --- **Stealth** +18 (expert) **Disable** DC 26 [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=34) to scramble out of the way, DC 24 [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=38) or [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=40) (trained) to draw the Ox’s attention. The DC of the [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333) for this round (see Routine) is increased by 4 on a success, or by 8 on a critical success. Increasing the flat check DC to 21 or higher buys the party enough time to move up the Ox’s back, disabling the hazard. **Tail Swat** **Trigger** A creature lands near the base of the Granite Ox’s tail; **Effect** The Granite Ox makes a tail Strike against the triggering creature. The hazard then rolls initiative. --- **Routine** (1 action) The Granite Ox makes a tail Strike against one creature in the area. If the attack succeeds, the GM rolls a DC 9 [flat check](/Rules.aspx?ID=333). On a success, the hazard makes another Strike. The hazard continues making Strikes until the GM fails the flat check.
**Melee** tail +20, Damage 2d10+11 bludgeoning plus [clumsy](/Conditions.aspx?ID=61) 1 for 1 round; no multiple attack penalty --- **Reset** Once all of the PCs moved outside the tail’s striking range, the hazard is effectively disabled. The hazard reactivates if any PC returns to that area.

fields.disable: Survival DC 25 (expert) to disturb the surface and reveal the tar pit
fields.markdown:
**Source** [Pathfinder #177: Burning Tundra](/Sources.aspx?ID=116) pg. 34 **Complexity** Complex A 15-foot-wide patch of tar covered with dirt and leaves attempts to capture creatures that step onto it. --- **Stealth** DC 30 (expert) **Disable** [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) DC 25 (expert) to disturb the surface and reveal the tar pit **Capture** **Trigger** A Huge or smaller creature walks onto the tar pit; **Effect** The triggering creature sinks into the tar pit up to its waist. The tar pit rolls initiative if it hasn't already. --- **Routine** (1 action) On its initiative, the tar pit pulls down each creature within it, thick tar adhering to the creature's body. A creature that was submerged up to its waist becomes submerged up to its neck, and a creature that was submerged up to its neck is pulled under and must hold its breath to avoid [suffocation](/Rules.aspx?ID=468).
A creature in the tar pit can attempt a DC 33 [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check to [Climb](/Actions.aspx?ID=33) to either raise itself by one step (if it's submerged to its neck or full submerged) or to move 5 feet if it's submerged only up to its waist. On a critical failure, the creature is pulled down one step. Other creatures can [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) the creature, typically by using a rope or similar aid or by attempting to pull the creature out with their own DC 33 Athletics check, with the same results as if the creature attempted the check. In addition to the usual results, a character adjacent to the tar pit who critically fails while Aiding moves into the tar pit. A creature that Climbs out of the tar pit escapes the hazard and lands prone in an adjacent space. --- **Reset** Though the hazard still captures anyone who touches it, the surface doesn't become hidden again until it settles, which takes 24 hours.
